section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, into which lane should you complete the turn?
options: a:In the right lane of the street.,b:In the center of the street.,c:In the left lane of the street.
note: When turning left from a two-way onto a one-way street, complete the turn into the lane nearest the lane you came from — typically the left lane.

question: If you are involved in an accident and another person is injured, you should:
options: a:Move the injured immediately away from the scene.,b:Always leave the injured where they are without rendering aid.,c:Not move the injured unless necessary, keep them warm, and provide first aid if you are trained.,d:Drive to the nearest hospital leaving the scene.
note: Avoid moving injured victims unless there is an immediate danger; keep them warm and give first aid within your training until emergency help arrives.

question: Which action should you take before making a turn?
options: a:Use your signal.,b:Turn the wheel immediately without signaling.,c:Increase your speed.
note: Signal at least three to four seconds before turning to notify other drivers and pedestrians of your intent.

question: Driving at night requires extra caution because:
options: a:Traffic moves faster at night.,b:There is a larger volume of traffic at night.,c:Drivers cannot see as well at night.,d:Headlights are not required at night.
note: Reduced light conditions limit visibility; use headlights from half an hour after sunset to half an hour before sunrise and increase your following distance.

question: What lane entitlement do motorcycles have?
options: a:Half the width of a lane.,b:The bicycle lane only.,c:The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to the full width of a traffic lane like any other vehicle.

question: When it starts to rain while you are driving, you should:
options: a:Turn on your headlights and slow down.,b:Drive at the posted speed limit at all times.,c:Speed up to pass other vehicles.
note: Reduce your speed, turn on low beam headlights in rain to increase visibility, and pull off if conditions become unsafe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a highway from an entrance ramp, you should generally:
options: a:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a large gap.,b:Enter slowly well below traffic speed.,c:Accelerate on the ramp to match the speed of freeway traffic and merge when safe.,d:Signal and stay on the ramp until traffic clears completely.
note: Use the acceleration lane to pick up speed and merge into an appropriate gap in traffic; the vehicles on the freeway have the right-of-way.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What color line divides lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions?
options: a:Yellow,b:Red,c:Black
note: Yellow pavement markings divide traffic moving in opposite directions; white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction.

question: When you see or hear an approaching emergency vehicle, what is the correct response on a two-lane road?
options: a:Stop immediately where you are.,b:Drive as far right as is safe and stop.,c:Proceed slowly and try to move out of its way later.
note: On two-lane roads, pull as far to the right as is safe and stop to allow emergency vehicles to pass.

question: Which of the following can impair driving and lead to DUII charges?
options: a:Controlled substances such as illegal drugs or certain prescription medicines.,b:Inhalants such as glue or paint.,c:Beer, wine, and other liquor.
note: A variety of substances—alcohol, illegal drugs, inhalants, and many prescription or over-the-counter medications—can impair driving.

question: If your accelerator becomes stuck while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Shift to neutral and apply steady pressure on the brake.,b:Reach down and try to pull the pedal up.,c:Shift to park immediately.
note: If the accelerator sticks, keep eyes on the road, shift to neutral, apply steady braking, pull off the road when safe, then turn off the engine.

question: What causes 'highway hypnosis'?
options: a:Driving after too much sleep the night before your trip.,b:Frequent rest stops.,c:Staring at the roadway for long periods and failing to scan.
note: Highway hypnosis can occur when you stare straight ahead for long periods and stop actively scanning; take breaks and keep your eyes moving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before turning left at an intersection, what must you do?
options: a:Sound your horn.,b:Yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,c:Swing to the right side of your lane.
note: When turning left, you must yield the right-of-way to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians before completing the turn.

question: If you approach a railroad crossing with flashing warning signals, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and look for a train.,b:Stop and look for a train.,c:Look for a train and then speed up across the tracks.
note: When warning signals are flashing you must stop (no closer than 15 feet from the rail) and remain stopped until safe to cross.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes on a highway, which actions should you take?
options: a:Check your rearview and outside mirrors.,b:Signal well in advance of the lane change.,c:Glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
note: When changing lanes, signal your intent, check mirrors for approaching traffic, and glance over your shoulder to ensure the blind spot is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, which vehicle must yield?
options: a:Drivers must make hand motions to communicate with each other.,b:The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.,c:The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.
note: When two vehicles reach a four-way stop simultaneously, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

question: The most important speed-management rule for curves is to:
options: a:Drive at the posted speed and brake at the sharpest part.,b:Slow down before entering the curve.,c:Accelerate into the curve to maintain momentum.,d:Brake sharply as you exit the curve.
note: Slow down before you enter a curve; adjusting speed in the curve is difficult and entering too fast can cause loss of control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before passing on a multilane highway you should:
options: a:Watch for oncoming traffic.,b:Pass only on the right.,c:Be sure the passing lane is clear.
note: Before passing, make sure the passing lane is clear, signal, and only pass when it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do if you approach an intersection that is blocked by traffic ahead?
options: a:Enter the intersection slowly and wait.,b:Get as close as possible to the car in front of you.,c:Stay out of the intersection until you can completely pass through.
note: Do not enter an intersection unless you can clear it; blocking intersections is illegal and unsafe.

question: Why should you avoid following another vehicle too closely?
options: a:You may not see the road between the cars.,b:You may not have enough time to stop if the vehicle ahead slows or stops suddenly.,c:You may not see the vehicle's turn signals.
note: Following too closely reduces the time and distance you have to react and stop, increasing the risk of a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If traffic signals at an intersection are not working due to a power outage, how should you treat the intersection?
options: a:Treat the intersection as a four-way stop and yield accordingly.,b:Use hand signals to indicate your intentions to other drivers.,c:Turn on your hazard lights and proceed without stopping.
note: When traffic lights are out, treat the intersection like a four-way stop: stop, yield in order, and proceed with caution.

question: To prepare for anything coming up on the road ahead you should:
options: a:Stare straight ahead at all times.,b:Drive with your left foot lightly on the brake.,c:Continually scan the entire road and roadsides.,d:Only look directly in front of your vehicle.
note: Search the roadway and sides continuously to identify hazards early and give yourself time to react.

question: Drinking alcohol and then driving is:
options: a:Safe if you have had only a few drinks.,b:A serious traffic safety problem.,c:A minor traffic safety problem.,d:A private matter for the driver.
note: Driving after drinking alcohol is a serious traffic safety hazard — alcohol and other drugs impair judgment and reaction time, making safe driving impossible.

question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the centerline mean?
options: a:You may pass with caution.,b:Do not pass.,c:Slow down immediately.
note: A solid yellow line next to your lane indicates that passing is prohibited from your direction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning or changing lanes, when must you signal?
options: a:Always, even if no visible traffic is present.,b:Only if there is visible traffic.,c:Only when driving at night.
note: You must signal every time you change lanes, turn, or pull away from a curb, regardless of visible traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection where two vehicles arrive simultaneously, who must yield?
options: a:The largest vehicle.,b:The car on the left has the right-of-way.,c:The car on the left must yield to the car on the right.
note: If two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does the driver's left arm and hand extended downward signal mean?
options: a:Turn left.,b:Turn right.,c:Stop.
note: A left arm extended downward is a hand signal indicating the vehicle is slowing or stopping.

question: A driver with a BAC between which levels is presumed to be Driving While Ability is Impaired (DWAI) in Colorado?
options: a:0.03 and 0.05 percent,b:0.05 and 0.07 percent,c:0.07 and 0.09 percent,d:0.09 and 0.11 percent
note: In Colorado, a BAC between 0.05% and 0.07% is presumed to be Driving While Ability is Impaired (DWAI), with associated legal consequences.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are required to stop your vehicle when:
options: a:Approaching an intersection with a stop sign.,b:Where there is a red light.,c:When a traffic officer orders you to stop.,d:All of the above.
note: You must stop at stop signs, red lights (including flashing red), or whenever a traffic officer directs you to stop.

question: How should drivers respond to a flashing red traffic signal?
options: a:Drive carefully without stopping.,b:Come to a complete stop, yield, and proceed when safe.,c:Merge to the right.
note: A flashing red signal means stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe — it functions like a stop sign.

question: Drowsy drivers can:
options: a:Stay alert by opening a window and turning up the radio.,b:Drive so poorly that they may appear to be drunk.,c:Be made fully alert by drinking coffee.,d:Drive better than well-rested drivers.
note: Drowsiness can impair driving similarly to alcohol impairment; opening a window or drinking coffee are not reliable countermeasures.

question: Which factor does stopping distance NOT depend on?
options: a:The condition of your vehicle's brakes.,b:Your own reaction time.,c:The time of day.
note: Stopping distance depends on reaction time, vehicle weight, brake and tire condition, roadway conditions, visibility, and speed — not the time of day.

question: What is the effect of combining drugs with alcohol on driving risk?
options: a:Is no more dangerous than consuming alcohol by itself.,b:Increases the risk of causing a crash.,c:Lessens the effect of alcohol on your ability to drive.
note: Combining alcohol with other drugs (prescription, over-the-counter, or illegal) can increase impairment and the risk of a crash.

question: Pennant-shaped traffic signs typically indicate:
options: a:School zones.,b:No passing zones.,c:Speed limits.,d:Railroad crossings.
note: Pennant-shaped signs (sideways triangles) are used to mark no passing zones; additional text or pavement markings may confirm this.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If another vehicle is passing you, what should you do to help them pass safely?
options: a:Pull off the road to let them pass.,b:Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed to allow safe passing.,c:Flash your lights to signal them to hurry.
note: Keep right and, if safe, adjust your speed slightly to allow the passing vehicle to return to your lane safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When are you allowed to cross double solid yellow lines?
options: a:To pass another car.,b:To turn into a driveway.,c:To pass a slow-moving truck.
note: Double solid yellow lines prohibit passing; you may cross them to make a left turn into or from driveways, alleys, or to enter/exit the roadway where permitted.

question: If a driver accumulates how many points in a 12-month period will the license be suspended?
options: a:Five points,b:Ten points,c:Twelve points,d:Eighteen points
note: Colorado drivers who accrue 12 or more points within a 12-month period may face suspension of their driver license.

question: If a HAWK pedestrian signal is solid red, what must drivers do?
options: a:Slow down and prepare to stop.,b:Proceed with caution.,c:Come to a complete stop.
note: A solid red HAWK signal means drivers must stop and remain stopped until the signal changes and it is safe to proceed.

question: What should you do if an aggressive driver is following you closely?
options: a:Make eye contact and stare as they pass.,b:Speed up to prevent them from passing.,c:Move out of the aggressive driver’s way when safe.
note: If someone is driving aggressively, safely get out of their way, avoid eye contact, and do not escalate the situation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you have a green light but pedestrians are crossing against the red, you should:
options: a:Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrians.,b:Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.,c:Honk your horn to warn them.,d:Drive through carefully without stopping.
note: You must yield to pedestrians in the intersection even when you have a green light; stop and let them cross safely.

question: The best way to handle a tailgater is to:
options: a:Speed up to put more distance between you and the tailgater.,b:Slam on your brakes briefly to warn the tailgater.,c:Change lanes or gradually slow down to encourage the tailgater to pass.,d:Flash your lights repeatedly to signal them.
note: If someone is following too closely, safely change lanes or gently slow to encourage them to pass; do not brake check or speed up.

question: What may happen if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medications?
options: a:The medicine reduces the effect of the alcohol.,b:The combination could multiply the effects of the alcohol or medicine.,c:The alcohol will help the medicine cure a cold.
note: Mixing alcohol and many medications can amplify impairment and produce unpredictable or dangerous effects.

question: Who is required by law to wear a fastened safety belt in a moving vehicle?
options: a:The driver only.,b:Passengers in the front seat only.,c:Children between the ages of 8 and 18 only.,d:The driver, front-seat passengers, and all children 8–18 regardless of seating position.
note: Colorado law requires that drivers and front-seat passengers wear safety belts, and that children ages 8–18 be properly restrained wherever they are seated in the vehicle.

question: When backing up your vehicle, what is the recommended technique?
options: a:Rely only on your mirrors.,b:Turn your head and look through the rear window while backing.,c:Open your door to check behind the vehicle.
note: When reversing, turn your head and look through the rear window while also checking mirrors and surroundings; do not depend solely on mirrors or sensors.

question: What should you adjust first when getting into a vehicle to drive?
options: a:Your rearview mirror,b:Your seat,c:The steering wheel
note: When preparing to drive, first adjust your seat so you can reach the controls comfortably and see the road; then adjust mirrors and the steering wheel.

question: How should a lap belt fit?
options: a:Loose across your waist.,b:Buckled snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.,c:Tucked under the seat for comfort.
note: A lap belt should fit snugly across your hip bones and the lower part of your abdomen; shoulder belts should lie comfortably across the chest.

question: How can stress affect your driving?
options: a:Causing you to fall asleep at the wheel.,b:Lowering your ability to focus on driving.,c:Decreasing your chances of an accident.,d:Improving reaction time.
note: Strong emotions or stress can reduce your concentration and impair your ability to drive safely; it is best to avoid driving while emotionally unstable.

question: Which is not permitted for a passenger in a moving motor vehicle?
options: a:Have an opened alcohol container.,b:Sleep.,c:Use a cell phone.,d:Listen to music.
note: It is unlawful for passengers to drink from or possess an open alcoholic beverage container in the passenger area of a motor vehicle on a public road.

question: When stopped by law enforcement for a traffic violation, what must the driver present?
options: a:Proof of registration.,b:Their license.,c:Proof of insurance.
note: When stopped, the driver must present a valid driver license and, when requested, proof of vehicle registration and insurance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must not drive faster than:
options: a:The posted maximum speed limit.,b:A speed that is faster than is reasonable and prudent for current conditions.,c:A speed that is safe for existing road, traffic, and weather conditions.,d:All of the above.
note: You must obey posted limits, but also drive at a speed that is reasonable and prudent given road, traffic, weather, and visibility conditions.

question: When changing lanes you should NOT do which of the following?
options: a:Fail to check side and rearview mirrors and blind spots.,b:Signal your intentions.,c:Check for other drivers who may also be moving into the same lane.
note: Never change lanes without checking mirrors and blind spots; always signal and check for other drivers before moving over.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do when entering a roadway from a private road or driveway?
options: a:Drive out fast to merge smoothly with the traffic.,b:Yield to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway.,c:Blow your horn to warn cars you are entering the roadway.
note: When entering a roadway from a private road or driveway, yield the right-of-way to all pedestrians and vehicles on the roadway.

question: If your car breaks down on a highway, you should:
options: a:Sit in your car and wait for help without signaling.,b:Sound your horn at passing motorists to get attention.,c:Use your hazard (four-way) flashers and move well off the road, then signal and exit safely.,d:Walk along the highway to find help.
note: If your vehicle is disabled, get as far off the roadway as possible, turn on your hazard lights, lift the hood, and stay where other drivers can see you until help arrives.

question: Crosswalks are:
options: a:Always indicated only by horizontal pavement markings.,b:Always indicated by vertical markings.,c:Present whether marked or unmarked and must be respected.,d:Always unmarked.
note: Crosswalks exist with or without painted lines; drivers must yield to pedestrians and stop behind the crosswalk when required.

question: When you see a flashing yellow arrow for left turns, what does it mean?
options: a:You may turn left only after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:You must come to a complete stop before turning.,c:You should merge into the lane indicated by the arrow before turning.
note: A flashing yellow arrow allows left turns but requires you to yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians before turning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which action should you take before changing lanes or passing on an interstate?
options: a:Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots.,b:Stop on the shoulder of the road if you are tired.,c:You should always use cruise control.
note: Before changing lanes or passing on an interstate, signal, check your mirrors, and glance to check blind spots; only stop on the shoulder for emergencies.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning onto a street with multiple lanes in your direction, into which lane should you turn?
options: a:Turn into the middle lane.,b:Turn into the lane closest to your previous lane.,c:Turn into the lane marked with an arrow.
note: When turning onto a street with more than one lane moving in the same direction, enter the lane closest to the lane you came from and avoid lane changes during the turn.

question: What does a solid red arrow on a traffic signal mean?
options: a:Is never used as a traffic signal.,b:Has the same meaning as a circular red traffic light.,c:Means drivers may turn in the direction indicated by the arrow.
note: A solid red arrow means the same as a steady red light: traffic in the indicated lane must stop and may not turn in the arrow's direction.

question: You may cross solid yellow center lines:
options: a:To pass traffic moving in the same direction.,b:Only during daylight hours.,c:Only to make a turn into or out of a driveway or side road.,d:At any time for passing.
note: Solid yellow lines generally prohibit passing; you may cross a solid yellow line to turn into a driveway, alley, or side road when safe and permitted.

question: What happens to your tires' effectiveness on a wet roadway as your speed increases?
options: a:They become less effective at clearing water and can lead to hydroplaning.,b:Water does not affect cars with good tires.,c:Deep water is less dangerous than shallow water.
note: Higher speeds reduce tires' ability to clear water from the road, increasing hydroplaning risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a two-way, two-lane road you cannot pass safely unless:
options: a:You can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.,b:You are able to clearly see the road ahead.,c:Your vehicle is capable of the speed necessary to complete the pass.,d:All of the above.
note: Passing on a two-lane, two-way road is only safe if you can see far enough ahead, complete the pass before meeting oncoming traffic, and have sufficient vehicle speed to pass safely.

question: If your wheels slip off the edge of the pavement, you should:
options: a:Jerk the steering wheel to force the vehicle back onto the pavement.,b:Slow down by gently applying the brakes and steer back onto the pavement when safe.,c:Slam on your brakes immediately.,d:Speed up and swerve onto the pavement.
note: Keep control by slowing gradually while wheels are off the pavement; when you can do so safely, steer back onto the road — do not make sudden turns.

question: When passing a large truck or bus, what should drivers of smaller vehicles be prepared for?
options: a:Loud noises.,b:Excess air pollution.,c:Wind gusts produced by the large vehicle.,d:No effect on vehicle stability.
note: Large vehicles can create strong air gusts that may affect small vehicles' stability; be ready to correct steering when approaching or passing them.

question: Compared to daytime driving, driving at night is:
options: a:Less dangerous.,b:No more or less dangerous.,c:More dangerous.
note: Night driving is more hazardous due to reduced visibility, glare from lights, and an increased likelihood of tired or impaired drivers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a divided multilane highway, if you hear or see an approaching emergency vehicle, you should:
options: a:Stop immediately where you are regardless of lanes.,b:Disregard the signal if other lanes are available.,c:Slow down, move to provide a clear path, and stop if necessary.,d:Speed up to stay out of its way.
note: Yield to emergency vehicles by slowing and moving aside to create a clear path; do not attempt to outrun or block them.

question: What does a solid black HAWK signal indicate to drivers?
options: a:Drivers should come to a complete stop.,b:Drivers may proceed past the crosswalk with caution.,c:Drivers should slow down and prepare to stop.
note: A HAWK signal that goes dark (solid black) means drivers may proceed past the crosswalk with caution but should watch for pedestrians.

question: What does a single dashed white line mean between lanes?
options: a:Drivers may pass or change lanes if it is safe.,b:Lanes move in opposite directions.,c:Drivers are not allowed to pass.
note: A dashed white line separates lanes traveling in the same direction and may be crossed to pass or change lanes when safe.

question: If an approaching train is near enough or going fast enough to be a danger, you must:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution across the tracks.,b:Not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.,c:Cross the tracks if there is no ground-level light signal.,d:Weave through railroad gates if you are in a hurry.
note: If a train poses a potential danger, do not attempt to cross; wait until it has fully passed and it is safe to proceed.

question: If you become too drowsy to focus while driving, the safest action is to:
options: a:Drink a large energy drink.,b:Open the windows and turn on the air conditioning.,c:Pull off the road and rest.,d:Continue driving slowly until help is found.
note: Drowsiness greatly reduces reaction time and decision-making. If you feel too tired to drive safely, stop in a safe location and rest.

question: When driving to an unfamiliar area, you should:
options: a:Depend solely on road signs to find your way.,b:Plan your route in advance.,c:Rely only on general knowledge of the area.,d:Drive faster to avoid getting lost.
note: Plan your route ahead of time, study maps or GPS directions, and allow extra time so you can drive safely without last-minute maneuvers.

question: What color are signs indicating areas of public recreation or cultural interest?
options: a:Red.,b:Brown.,c:Green.
note: Brown guide signs indicate parks, recreation areas, historical sites, and other cultural or recreational points of interest.

question: What should you do to help prevent crashes with other road users?
options: a:Ignore other drivers and focus only on your vehicle.,b:Communicate with other road users using signals or horn when appropriate.,c:Drive only on side streets and back roads.
note: Communicate intent to other road users by signaling, using lights or horn appropriately, and driving predictably to reduce misunderstandings.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a steady green traffic light allow you to do?
options: a:Stop and check for oncoming traffic before proceeding.,b:May drive through the intersection if it is clear.,c:Must slow down and prepare to stop.
note: A steady green light means you may proceed through the intersection when the way is clear; when turning, you must yield to pedestrians and other traffic.

question: Which is the safest way to drive through a curve?
options: a:Speed up as you enter and slow down as you exit.,b:Maintain the same speed throughout.,c:Slow down entering the curve and accelerate gradually as you exit.
note: Enter curves at a reduced speed and accelerate gradually as you exit to maintain control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing from the right lane into the left lane on a multilane highway, you should:
options: a:Look in your rearview mirror only for traffic behind you.,b:Look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot and signal your intention.,c:Turn on your directional signal and move left without looking.,d:Assume no one is beside you if your mirrors appear clear.
note: Check mirrors and then glance over your shoulder into the blind spot for the lane you intend to enter; always signal before changing lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two drivers arrive at an open intersection at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on the left.,b:The driver on the right.,c:Either driver may continue without stopping.
note: If you and another vehicle arrive simultaneously at an open intersection, yield to the vehicle on your right.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, you should:
options: a:Rely solely on your mirrors.,b:Begin signaling only as you move into the next lane.,c:Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes and glance over your shoulder to check the blind spot.,d:Signal 500 feet before changing lanes in residential areas.
note: Signal early (about 100 feet in many situations), check mirrors, and glance over your shoulder to ensure the lane is clear of vehicles in your blind spot.

question: If a vehicle using high beams approaches, where should you direct your gaze?
options: a:The center of the road.,b:Either side of the road.,c:The right side of the road.
note: Glance toward the right edge of the road to avoid being blinded by approaching high beams until the vehicle passes.

question: In rainy driving conditions which headlights should you use?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights only.
note: Use low beam headlights in rain, fog, or snow; high beams can reflect and reduce visibility.

question: If there are two railroad tracks next to each other, you should:
options: a:Assume it is safe to cross once one train passes.,b:Always stop before every set of tracks.,c:Look for a second train on the other track after one passes before you proceed.,d:Drive faster to beat the next train.
note: When multiple tracks exist, wait and look for any other approaching trains on the adjacent tracks before you begin crossing.

question: At a multi-track railroad crossing where you have stopped, what should you do after a train passes?
options: a:Go through as soon as the train passes.,b:Wait until you have a clear view of all tracks before proceeding.,c:Stop on the first track and watch for another train.
note: When multiple tracks exist, wait until you can see all tracks clearly before crossing; another train may be approaching on a different track.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking downhill on a two-way street, which way should you point your front wheels?
options: a:Turn your wheels to the left.,b:Turn your wheels to the right.,c:Keep your wheels pointed straight ahead.
note: When parked facing downhill, turn your wheels toward the curb or side of the road so the vehicle will roll away from traffic if it moves.

question: Compared with smaller cars, larger vehicles generally have:
options: a:Larger blind spots.,b:No blind spots.,c:Smaller blind spots.
note: The larger the vehicle, the larger its blind spots — trucks and large SUVs have areas around the rear and sides that can’t be seen in mirrors.

question: What single action most reduces your risk of serious injury or death in a crash?
options: a:Limit your driving to weekdays.,b:Wear your seat belt.,c:Stay in the right lane on multilane highways.
note: Wearing a properly fastened seat belt is the most effective way to reduce risk of injury or death in a traffic crash.

question: How must license plates be displayed?
options: a:Fastened so they cannot swing.,b:Folded for storage when not needed.,c:Placed vertically instead of horizontally.
note: License plates must be mounted horizontally, clearly visible, kept clean, and fastened to prevent swinging; typically at least 12 inches from the ground.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection with a yield sign you should:
options: a:Always come to a full stop regardless of other traffic.,b:Slow down and yield the right-of-way to traffic in the intersection or roadway you are entering.,c:Yield only to traffic approaching from the left.,d:Proceed at the same speed unless another vehicle is present.
note: A yield sign requires you to slow and yield to any traffic or pedestrians in the roadway you are entering; stop if necessary to avoid conflict.

question: A person's ability to drive can be impaired by which of the following?
options: a:Alcohol.,b:Any medication (prescription or over-the-counter),c:Lack of sleep.,d:All of the above.
note: Alcohol, many medications (legal and illegal), and drowsiness can all impair driving ability and should be considered before driving.

question: If you need to slow down on a slippery road, what should you do first?
options: a:Firmly apply your brakes.,b:Take your foot off the gas.,c:Apply your parking brake.
note: On a slippery surface, first take your foot off the accelerator; if more slowing is needed, apply brakes gently and steadily.

question: Which signal requires coming to a complete stop, yielding to cross traffic/pedestrians, then proceeding when clear?
options: a:Flashing yellow light.,b:Solid red light.,c:Flashing red light.
note: A flashing red signal should be treated like a stop sign: stop, yield to cross traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when safe.

question: How does alcohol affect your driving skills and judgment?
options: a:It helps driving skills but harms judgment.,b:It has no effect on either driving skills or judgment.,c:It harms both driving skills and judgment.
note: Alcohol impairs multiple driving-related abilities, including reaction time, coordination, vision, concentration, and judgement.

question: What does a red arrow on a traffic signal mean?
options: a:Proceed slowly through the intersection.,b:Stop and remain stopped until the signal changes to a green light or green arrow.,c:Stop and then proceed when the way is clear.
note: A red arrow means you must stop and remain stopped until the signal changes to a green light or green arrow (unless otherwise posted).

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an officer is directing traffic at an intersection with a working traffic signal, drivers should:
options: a:Always follow the traffic signal instead of the officer.,b:Follow the directions given by the officer.,c:Honk to get the officer’s attention.,d:Proceed only when the light allows it.
note: When a police officer is directing traffic, you must obey the officer's directions even if they conflict with the traffic signals.

question: Which activities are common causes of distracted driving?
options: a:Changing a radio station or CD.,b:Talking or texting on a phone.,c:Eating, drinking, or smoking.
note: Distracted driving includes many tasks such as eating, using a phone, or changing audio controls — all of which reduce attention to driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you slow down when exiting a highway?
options: a:On the main road, just before the exit lane.,b:Once you see a toll booth.,c:Once you have moved into the exit lane.,d:Before entering the exit lane.
note: Enter the exit lane well in advance and begin braking and slowing only after you are in the exit lane.

question: Which statement about seat belts and child restraints is correct?
options: a:An airbag can be dangerous to an infant or small child in a front-facing seat.,b:You should never place an infant or small child in the rear seat.,c:You should always make sure all passengers are using a seat belt or child restraint.
note: Always make sure everyone is properly restrained; children 12 and under should ride in the rear seat and never place a rear-facing infant seat in a front seat with an active airbag.

question: Which of the following commonly causes traffic accidents?
options: a:Inattentive driving.,b:Following other vehicles too closely.,c:Excessive speed under the driving conditions.,d:Rare vehicle defects.
note: Distracted or inattentive driving is a leading cause of crashes; excessive speed and following too closely are also common contributing factors.

question: How should you act when approaching the scene of an accident while driving?
options: a:Keep your attention on your driving.,b:Keep moving.,c:Stop if you are involved or if emergency help has not yet arrived.
note: Do not stop at an accident scene unless you are directly involved or are needed and emergency help has not arrived; keep your attention on safe driving.

question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, how should you respond?
options: a:Flash your vehicle's lights to let them know they are wrong.,b:Call the police immediately.,c:Stay calm and move out of their way.
note: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, remain calm and get out of their way. Escalating the situation increases danger for everyone.

question: A solid white line on the right edge of the highway that slants to the left indicates:
options: a:The road ahead will be narrower.,b:An intersection is just ahead.,c:A construction area is ahead.,d:You will be required to turn left soon.
note: An edge line that angles toward the center of the road warns that the roadway narrows ahead; keep a safe position within the travel lane.

question: What best ensures safety when you back your vehicle?
options: a:Honk your horn before shifting into reverse.,b:Walk around and check behind the vehicle before getting in.,c:Only check rearview mirrors after getting in.
note: Before backing, walk to the rear of the vehicle to check for children, objects, or other hazards you might not see from the driver's seat.

question: How can you avoid being in a truck or bus driver's blind spot?
options: a:Avoid driving alongside them and do not tailgate.,b:Never pass them under any circumstances.,c:Flash your lights at them to get their attention.
note: Avoid lingering alongside large vehicles and avoid tailgating so drivers can always see you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you enter freeway traffic from an on-ramp?
options: a:Signal, yield to existing traffic, and enter at the same speed that traffic is moving.,b:Signal and enter the freeway; freeway traffic must yield.,c:Drive slowly so you can check traffic.
note: When merging, accelerate on the ramp as needed, signal, yield to mainline traffic, and merge at approximately the speed of traffic.

question: When driving in bad weather, you should:
options: a:Increase your following distance.,b:Increase your speed to pass hazards quickly.,c:Decrease your following distance.,d:Turn off headlights during heavy rain.
note: In adverse weather you should slow down and increase your following distance, since stopping distances increase on wet or icy roads.

question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?
options: a:Replace tires with bad tread.,b:Do not speed when the roads are wet.,c:Use tires with proper air pressure.
note: To reduce hydroplaning risk, avoid speeding on wet roads, maintain proper tire pressure, and replace tires with poor tread.

question: After stopping for a school bus that is unloading children, what should you do?
options: a:Accelerate quickly.,b:Watch for children walking along the side of the road.,c:Do not proceed until the children wave to you.
note: After a school bus has stopped with its stop arm extended and lights flashing, watch carefully for children walking along the road before proceeding.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing without flashing signals or gates, you should:
options: a:Cross immediately and as quickly as possible.,b:Always stop before crossing.,c:Be prepared to yield to any approaching train.
note: When there are no automatic warnings, slow, look both ways, and be prepared to yield; never enter unless you can clear the tracks.

question: Which of the following does NOT promote safe night driving?
options: a:Keep your windshield clean.,b:Be aware that tinted windows reduce visibility at night.,c:Carry a flashlight inside your vehicle at all times.,d:Stare directly into oncoming headlights to adjust your vision.
note: Avoid looking into oncoming headlights. Keep windshields clean and be aware that heavy tinting reduces night visibility; a flashlight is useful but staring into headlights is unsafe.

question: A speed advisory sign attached to a curve means:
options: a:You should reduce speed below the advisory in rainy, snowy, or icy conditions.,b:The sign has a triangular shape.,c:The sign is blue with black lettering.,d:You may ignore the advisory if you drive carefully.
note: Advisory speeds recommend safe speeds under normal conditions; in poor weather you should reduce speed even further than the advisory.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking uphill next to a curb, what should you do after setting the parking brake?
options: a:Keep the front tires straight ahead.,b:Keep the rear tires against the curb.,c:Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn your wheels away from the curb so a roll would cause the front of the vehicle to roll into the curb.

question: If your vehicle's right wheels leave the pavement, what should you do first?
options: a:Accelerate and steer back onto the road quickly.,b:Immediately pull all the way off of the road and get back on when it is safe.,c:Stop quickly.
note: If your right wheels leave the pavement, ease off the accelerator, steer parallel to the road, slow down, then carefully steer back onto the pavement when safe.

question: What is the appropriate action approaching a railroad crossing that has no active signals?
options: a:Always bring the car to a complete stop.,b:Slow down and be prepared to stop.,c:All railroad crossings have signals so you will never encounter this situation.,d:Speed up and cross quickly.
note: At an unmarked or unsignaled railroad crossing, slow down, look both ways, listen for trains, and be prepared to stop if a train is approaching.

question: When driving through an area where children are playing, you should expect them to:
options: a:Know when it is safe to cross the street.,b:Stop at the curb before crossing.,c:Possibly run out into the street without looking.,d:Yield to vehicles at all times.
note: Children may act unpredictably and can run into the road without looking; slow down and be prepared to stop.

question: How are reversible lanes typically indicated?
options: a:Double broken yellow lines.,b:Double solid white lines.,c:Double solid yellow lines.
note: Reversible lanes may be marked by double broken yellow lines or by overhead lane-control signals indicating the current direction of travel.

question: If you are in a line of traffic crossing tracks with no signals or gates, what must you ensure?
options: a:You may pass slower drivers while on the tracks.,b:There is room for your vehicle to clear all tracks without stopping.,c:You have the right-of-way so you do not need to check for trains.
note: Ensure there is enough space ahead for your entire vehicle to clear all tracks before moving onto the rails; never stop on the tracks.

question: On which signal do you have the right-of-way to complete a left turn?
options: a:A flashing yellow light.,b:A green arrow pointing left.,c:A solid green light.
note: A green arrow pointing left is a protected turn signal and gives you the right-of-way to turn when the arrow is displayed.

question: As a pedestrian, which practice is recommended?
options: a:Always insist on the right-of-way over a vehicle when using a crosswalk.,b:Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching.,c:Enter a crosswalk at any time because it is the driver’s responsibility to stop.
note: Pedestrians should not step into a crosswalk when vehicles are approaching and unable to stop in time, even though drivers must yield.

question: If you must stop along the road at night, what should you do to remain visible?
options: a:Turn off all your lights.,b:Turn on your emergency flashers and keep low beam headlights on.,c:Use only your parking lights.
note: When stopped along the road at night, use your hazard lights and keep low beams on so other drivers can see your vehicle.

question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle with flashing red or blue lights is approaching?
options: a:Try to reach your destination before it arrives.,b:Continue driving and try to stay out of its way.,c:Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
note: Yield to emergency vehicles by pulling over to the right and stopping if it is safe to do so; if in an intersection, proceed through then pull over.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching an intersection displaying a flashing yellow light you should:
options: a:Stop and wait for the light to change.,b:Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.,c:Proceed through the intersection with caution.,d:Increase speed to clear the intersection quickly.
note: A flashing yellow light means proceed with caution — slow down and be alert for cross traffic or hazards.

question: A diamond-shaped traffic sign is used to:
options: a:Warn drivers of existing or possible hazards ahead.,b:Alert drivers to school zones.,c:Mark public recreation areas.,d:Indicate regulatory instructions like speed limits.
note: Diamond-shaped signs are warning signs that alert drivers to potential hazards or changes in road conditions ahead.

question: How should you check your blind spots before changing lanes?
options: a:Use only the inside rearview mirror.,b:Turn your head and glance over your shoulder into the blind spot.,c:Use only the outside rearview mirror.
note: Always turn your head and look over your shoulder to check blind spots before changing lanes — do not rely solely on mirrors.

question: A flashing red traffic signal is equivalent to which traffic device?
options: a:A solid red light.,b:Stop sign.,c:Yield sign.
note: A flashing red traffic signal has the same meaning as a stop sign: come to a complete stop, then proceed when safe.

question: A yellow and black diamond-shaped sign:
options: a:Warns you about conditions on or near the road ahead.,b:Directs you to cities and towns ahead.,c:Tells you about traffic laws and regulations.,d:Marks the beginning of a parking zone.
note: Diamond-shaped warning signs with black symbols on a yellow background alert drivers to road conditions or hazards ahead.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you pass your exit on an interstate, what should you do?
options: a:Continue driving and use the next exit.,b:Make a U-turn to go back to the exit.,c:Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.,d:Back up on the shoulder to reach the exit.
note: If you miss your exit on an interstate, drive to the next exit — do not make sudden turns, U-turns, or reverse on the highway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you yield to other drivers?
options: a:When they are on a road to your left and you have reached an unmarked intersection at the same time.,b:When entering a street from a garage or alley.,c:When your traffic signal is a green arrow.
note: You must yield when entering a street from an alley, driveway, or garage and to pedestrians on intersecting sidewalks.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it acceptable to proceed through an intersection showing a yellow light?
options: a:If you are already inside the intersection when the light turns yellow, proceed carefully.,b:If there is an emergency vehicle crossing your lane.,c:If pedestrians are crossing in the direction you are going.
note: If you are already in the intersection when a steady yellow appears, continue through carefully; otherwise, slow to stop if you can do so safely.

question: If you are involved in a traffic accident, what is the first thing you should do?
options: a:Stop immediately.,b:Call the police.,c:Help the injured.,d:Leave the scene.
note: Stop your vehicle at the scene if possible, move it out of traffic if safe, call police or emergency services as needed, and render aid without moving seriously injured persons unless necessary.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: The amount of space you need to cross traffic safely depends on:
options: a:Road and weather conditions and oncoming traffic.,b:Whether a stop sign is present.,c:Use of your turn signals.,d:The color of the vehicle you are driving.
note: Space required to cross traffic varies with road and weather conditions and the speed and distance of oncoming vehicles.

question: When driving near heavy trucks, fellow road users must allow for what characteristic of large vehicles?
options: a:The decreased noise of larger vehicles.,b:The increased stopping distance required by large vehicles.,c:The decreased stopping distance required by large vehicles.
note: Heavy trucks require much more distance to stop; other drivers should avoid lingering in a truck driver's blind spot and allow extra space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are impeding traffic by driving too slowly on a two-lane, two-way road, what should you do?
options: a:Decrease your speed.,b:Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.,c:Not let other cars pass your vehicle.
note: If traffic is backing up behind you on a two-lane road because you are driving significantly slower than the flow, pull over safely to let others pass.

question: What do orange-colored traffic signs generally indicate?
options: a:Railroad crossing ahead.,b:Construction, maintenance, or emergency operations.,c:A school zone ahead.
note: Orange signs with black symbols or lettering typically warn of construction, maintenance, or emergency operations ahead.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light at an intersection mean?
options: a:Stop and wait for green.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Continue normally through the intersection at full speed.
note: A flashing yellow light means use caution: slow down, look for hazards, and proceed carefully when safe.

question: If you are followed by a fire engine that is not using its emergency signals, how should you drive?
options: a:Continue to drive in a normal manner.,b:Speed up to get out of its way.,c:Stop as quickly as possible.
note: If an emergency vehicle behind you is not using lights or sirens, you do not need to clear the lane; continue driving normally.

question: What should you do when roads are slippery?
options: a:Drive the posted speed limit and be cautious.,b:Slow down.,c:Drive more quickly.
note: Reduce your speed at the first sign of rain, snow, or sleet; slippery conditions often require driving slower than the posted limit.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, you should turn the steering wheel:
options: a:To keep the front wheels straight.,b:In the direction you want the vehicle to go (into the skid),c:In the opposite direction of the skid.,d:Sharply in either direction to correct quickly.
note: If a skid occurs, steer in the direction you want the vehicle to go; as control returns, adjust steering back to straighten out.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do when you approach a steady red traffic light?
options: a:Stop; you may turn right after yielding if no sign prohibits it.,b:Drive through if there is no crossing traffic.,c:Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
note: A steady red light requires a complete stop. You may turn right on red unless a sign prohibits it, but you must yield to other traffic and pedestrians.

question: Where should you place your hands on the steering wheel for best control?
options: a:1 and 11 o'clock,b:2 and 10 o'clock,c:3 and 9 o'clock.
note: Place both hands on the outside of the wheel at roughly the 3 and 9 o’clock positions for the best control, especially with airbags.

question: If your power steering fails while driving, you should:
options: a:Honk your horn and turn off the engine immediately.,b:Turn on hazard lights and continue at the same speed.,c:Work harder to steer, reduce speed, and pull safely off the road as soon as possible.,d:Try to shift into neutral and coast to a stop in the travel lane.
note: Loss of power steering increases steering effort — slow down, signal, and move to a safe area off the road to stop and address the problem.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, you should:
options: a:Keep the front wheels straight and set the parking brake.,b:Turn the front wheels away from the curb (to the left) and set the brake.,c:Turn the front wheels toward the curb and leave in gear.,d:Leave the wheels turned toward the road center.
note: When parked uphill with a curb, turn your wheels away from the curb so the vehicle will roll away from traffic if the brakes fail.

question: If you are taking an over-the-counter medication, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Read the labels and warnings on the drug.,b:Drink alcohol instead to ease symptoms.,c:Ignore any warnings and drive as usual.
note: Many non-prescription medications can impair driving; read labels and warnings and consult a doctor or pharmacist if unsure.

question: If a HAWK pedestrian signal is flashing yellow, what should drivers do?
options: a:Drivers may proceed with caution.,b:Drivers should come to a complete stop.,c:Drivers should slow down and prepare to stop.
note: A flashing yellow HAWK signal tells drivers to slow and be prepared to stop for pedestrians; the steady or flashing red patterns provide other commands.

question: Under which circumstances must you stop at a railroad crossing?
options: a:When directed to stop by a flagger.,b:When control is by a posted stop sign.,c:When flashing red signals and gates are operating.
note: You must stop at railroad crossings when directed by a flagger or stop sign and when flashing red lights or gates are active; do not try to beat a train.

question: Which of the following can impair your driving ability?
options: a:Allergy medicines, b:Marijuana, c:Cold remedies, d:All of the above
note: Many types of drugs — including illegal drugs, prescription medications, and over-the-counter medicines — can impair driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which action should drivers take when preparing to turn left?
options: a:Move into the left lane.,b:Slow down gradually while checking the rearview mirror.,c:Watch for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.
note: When preparing to turn left, signal in advance, watch for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians, and ensure your path is clear.

question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic at a school zone, you must:
options: a:Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.,b:Copy what surrounding traffic is doing even if it differs.,c:Assume the guard is not authorized to direct traffic.
note: Always obey a crossing guard's directions in a school zone; they are there to protect students and pedestrians.

question: What do orange work zone signs indicate?
options: a:It is summer.,b:You must immediately stop and back up.,c:Less-than-ideal driving conditions are present.
note: Orange work zone signs warn of road work and possibly changed traffic patterns; use extra caution and reduce speed.

question: What are potential risks of worn or bald tires?
options: a:Are likely to hydroplane.,b:Can make turning more difficult.,c:Can increase your stopping distance.
note: Worn or bald tires increase stopping distance, make steering and turning more difficult, and raise the risk of hydroplaning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle on a two-lane road, when should you return to the right lane?
options: a:Remain in the left lane if you intend to turn left.,b:Return to the driving lane when there is enough room between you and the vehicle you passed.,c:Return to the right side of the roadway immediately.
note: On two-lane roads you must return to the right side when there is enough space between you and the vehicle you passed.

question: When is it appropriate to use your horn as a warning?
options: a:When passing a bicyclist.,b:When you see a child about to run into the street.,c:When traveling through an intersection.
note: Use your horn to warn others when you believe they do not see you, for example if a child appears about to run into the roadway.

question: Why should you be cautious when passing a bicycle?
options: a:Because you are moving faster than the bicycle.,b:Because the bicycle always has the right-of-way.,c:Because oncoming traffic may not see you pull out to pass.
note: Cyclists may swerve to avoid hazards and oncoming traffic might not see you when you move into the adjacent lane; pass with care and give ample space.

question: Which statement about passing motorcycles is true?
options: a:It is okay for drivers of other vehicles to follow motorcycles closely.,b:A motorcycle with two people on it is more balanced than one with one rider.,c:The driver of a passenger vehicle must change lanes completely when passing a motorcycle.,d:Motorcycles are not entitled to a full lane.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to the full width of a lane; when passing a motorcycle, a passenger vehicle must change lanes completely if possible to provide safe space.

question: What is the best long-term method to avoid hydroplaning?
options: a:Keep tires properly maintained with good tread.,b:Watch out for standing water but take no other actions.,c:Use cruise control in wet or slushy conditions.
note: Maintain proper tire tread and pressure and reduce speed in wet conditions; do not use cruise control when roadways are slick.

question: When should you increase your following distance?
options: a:When driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your view.,b:When exiting an expressway only.,c:When following a motorcycle only.
note: Increase following distance when visibility is reduced by large vehicles, in bad weather, heavy traffic, or when anyone is tailgating you.

question: Which statement best describes stopping in a travel lane?
options: a:You may make a U-turn or back up if you get on the wrong entrance ramp of the freeway.,b:You may stop to drop off passengers.,c:You should not stop in a travel lane for any reason.,d:You may stop to look up an address.
note: Do not stop in a travel lane. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road; if you miss an exit, go to the next one or find a safe place to turn around.

question: Signs that warn drivers about hazardous conditions are called what?
options: a:Regulatory signs.,b:Warning signs.,c:Information signs.
note: Warning signs (usually yellow or fluorescent) advise drivers of potential hazards ahead.

question: Drivers who have been drinking before driving:
options: a:Are always aware of the risks they are taking.,b:Do not have sufficient control of their body, mind, or vehicle.,c:Are better drivers because they are more careful than sober drivers.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that impairs judgment, vision, concentration, reaction time, and coordination. No amount of drinking is safe before driving.

question: What is the proper response to a tire blowout while driving?
options: a:Do not immediately use your brakes.,b:Gradually slow down and pull off the road.,c:Take your foot off the gas.
note: If a tire blows out, take your foot off the gas, avoid hard braking, gradually slow down, then pull off the road in a controlled manner.

question: What type of markings or symbols are used on some highways to direct drivers into the correct lanes for turning?
options: a:Arrows painted on lanes or posted on signs.,b:Flashing red lights over each lane.,c:White lines on the side of the road only.
note: Arrows painted on the roadway and posted turning-lane signs indicate which lanes are designated for turning or through travel.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an approaching emergency vehicle, you must:
options: a:Slow down until it has passed.,b:Motion for the emergency vehicle to pass.,c:Drive to the right-hand edge of the road and stop until it passes.,d:Keep driving and maintain your lane.
note: Yield the right-of-way to emergency vehicles using lights or sirens by pulling to the right and stopping; if in an intersection, clear it first then stop to the right.

question: What may happen when alcohol is combined with another drug?
options: a:The effects of both the alcohol and drug may be increased.,b:Nothing will happen.,c:The effects of both may be reduced.
note: Mixing alcohol with other drugs can increase or unpredictably change the impairing effects of both substances.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following statements about passing is true?
options: a:Use your mirrors and look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot when passing to the left.,b:Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes or passing.,c:Wait until you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror before returning to your lane.,d:All of the above.
note: When passing, signal early (at least 100 feet), check mirrors and blind spots, and do not return to your lane until you can see the passed vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a crowded freeway, what should you do to merge into traffic?
options: a:Use your side and rearview mirrors and check blind spots, b:Use the acceleration lane to match the speed of freeway traffic, c:Yield to traffic already on the freeway, d:All of the above.
note: When merging, accelerate on the ramp to freeway speed, check mirrors and blind spots, and yield to traffic already on the freeway.

question: When sharing the road with a truck, remember trucks generally:
options: a:Require longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.,b:Require less distance to stop on a downgrade.,c:Have smaller blind spots than cars.,d:Require no additional space when turning.
note: Because of their size and weight, trucks need more room to stop and maneuver than passenger vehicles; give them extra space.

question: What does a solid yellow arrow on a turn-control signal mean?
options: a:Means that drivers may turn in the direction indicated by the arrow.,b:Has the same meaning as a circular yellow traffic light.,c:Is never used as a traffic signal.
note: A solid yellow arrow means the same as a circular yellow light: the protected turn is ending and you should prepare to stop.

question: On a two-lane road without bicycle lanes, how should you pass a bicyclist traveling the same direction?
options: a:Do not pass until you come to a traffic signal or stop sign.,b:Slow down and wait until there is no opposing traffic, then pass with sufficient space.,c:Continue driving straight; it's the bicyclist’s responsibility to get out of your way.
note: Treat bicyclists like other vehicles when passing, leaving ample space (typically at least 3 feet) and only passing when it is safe and clear.

question: What is the 'No zone' in relation to large trucks and buses?
options: a:The area of blind spots around a truck or bus.,b:A reduced speed zone near trucks.,c:A lane reserved for large vehicles only.
note: The 'No zone' refers to the blind spots around large vehicles where smaller vehicles may be unseen by the truck or bus driver.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two vehicles arrive at an intersection from different highways at the same time, which vehicle must yield?
options: a:Either one.,b:The vehicle on the left.,c:The vehicle on the right.,d:The vehicle that arrived first.
note: When two vehicles arrive simultaneously, the driver on the left must yield the right-of-way to the driver on the right.

question: When sharing the road with large trucks, drivers should know that trucks:
options: a:Have large blind spots and require extra room to maneuver and stop.,b:Can stop more quickly than passenger vehicles.,c:Do not need more room to maneuver than passenger cars.,d:Have a smaller turning radius than passenger vehicles.
note: Large trucks have extensive blind spots and, due to their size and weight, require more space to stop and maneuver than passenger vehicles.

question: Which greatly increases stopping distances and the severity of crashes?
options: a:High speeds,b:Slow speeds,c:Night driving,d:Driving in neutral
note: Higher speeds increase stopping distance and crash severity; controlling speed helps reduce the risk and seriousness of collisions.

question: If you see an animal on the roadway, what should you do?
options: a:Pass the animal slowly to avoid startling it.,b:No special action is required.,c:Pass the animal as closely as possible.
note: Exercise caution, slow down, and pass animals slowly to avoid startling them and causing unpredictable movement.

question: Why must you use extra caution around a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog?
options: a:They may be deaf.,b:They are blind and may not see traffic.,c:They are crossing illegally.
note: A white cane or guide dog signals a blind pedestrian; yield to and exercise extra caution around them.

question: How should you handle turns on slick roads?
options: a:Change lanes quickly to avoid hazards.,b:Accelerate quickly before entering the turn.,c:Take turns more slowly than usual.
note: On slippery roads reduce speed before turns and curves; take turns more slowly than you would under normal conditions.

question: Before passing another vehicle, what should you do?
options: a:Check your mirrors and blind spots.,b:Honk your horn at least three times.,c:Re-enter your lane within 10 feet of the passed vehicle.,d:Flash your headlights repeatedly.
note: Before passing, check your mirrors and blind spots, signal, and only return to your lane when you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle using lights or siren, what must you do?
options: a:Keep driving in your lane.,b:Slow down and keep moving in your lane.,c:Pull to the right curb and stop.,d:Speed up to get out of the way.
note: When an emergency vehicle is approaching with lights or siren, you must immediately pull over to the curb or side of the road and stop until it has passed.

question: What should drivers do when approaching a traffic signal showing a steady yellow arrow?
options: a:Should merge into a lane in the direction of the arrow.,b:Should stop if it is safe to do so.,c:May turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,d:Proceed as if the arrow were green.
note: A steady yellow arrow means a red arrow is coming; drivers should stop unless they are already in the intersection and cannot safely stop.

question: At a light rail crossing, what must you always do?
options: a:Share the road with pedestrians and bicyclists.,b:Look both ways before crossing tracks and obey all traffic signals.,c:Drive around lowered gates if you can get through quickly.
note: Always look both ways before crossing tracks, obey signs and signals, and never drive around lowered crossing gates.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light tell you to do?
options: a:Merging traffic.,b:Proceed with caution.,c:Pedestrian crossing.
note: A flashing yellow signal means slow down and proceed with caution.

question: Many crashes are caused by which of the following?
options: a:Drivers traveling too fast for conditions.,b:Drivers consistently checking their mirrors and blind spots.,c:Drivers yielding the right-of-way.
note: Driving too fast for the current conditions is a frequent factor in crashes; always reduce speed when conditions are less than ideal.

question: On what road surfaces does your stopping distance increase?
options: a:On wet or icy roads.,b:On paved highways in perfect conditions.,c:Only when driving during the day.
note: Stopping distances increase on wet, icy, gravel, or otherwise slippery surfaces; drive slower and increase following distance.

question: If you are driving in another vehicle's blind spot, what should you do?
options: a:Keep a steady pace.,b:Stay in the driver's blind spot.,c:Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.
note: Avoid remaining in another driver's blind spot; either move ahead or fall back so the driver can see you in mirrors.

question: Your vehicle's brake lights tell other drivers that you are:
options: a:Changing lanes.,b:Making a turn.,c:Using your emergency brake.,d:Slowing down or stopping.
note: Brake lights signal to following drivers that you are slowing or stopping; keep them in working order to warn others of your actions.

question: Does drinking coffee after drinking alcohol reduce your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Cancels the effect of alcohol.,b:Decreases BAC.,c:Has no effect on BAC.
note: Coffee, fresh air, or other remedies do not reduce BAC; only time will metabolize alcohol out of your system.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Just before changing lanes, which check should you perform?
options: a:Quickly turn your head to check for other vehicles in your blind spot.,b:Check only the side view mirror.,c:Check the rearview mirror only.
note: When changing lanes check your mirrors for traffic and then glance over your shoulder to check the blind spot before moving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes on a multilane highway you should:
options: a:Sound your horn to alert other drivers.,b:Check rearview and side mirrors and look over your shoulder for blind spots.,c:Turn on your headlights to indicate a lane change.
note: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to make sure no one is in your blind spot, then signal and change lanes when safe.

question: If your accelerator sticks while driving, what is the correct immediate action?
options: a:Slam on your brakes.,b:Turn off the ignition and carefully pull off the road.,c:Blow your horn.
note: If the accelerator sticks, turn off the ignition (only enough to stop the engine without locking the steering), apply brakes, and steer the vehicle safely off the roadway.

question: Why must drivers be especially alert for motorcycles?
options: a:Motorcycles are more difficult to see than cars.,b:Motorcyclists do not have the same rights as other vehicles.,c:Motorcyclists rarely use headlights.
note: Because motorcycles are smaller and easier to hide in blind spots, it can be hard to judge their speed and distance; give them a full lane and extra caution.

question: Is it legal to cross a double solid yellow centerline to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Yes.,b:No.,c:Only if there is no oncoming traffic.
note: Double solid yellow lines prohibit crossing to pass; you may cross only to turn into a driveway or make a permitted turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver's left arm extended upward is a hand signal for:
options: a:Turning left.,b:Coming to a stop.,c:Turning right.
note: When a driver's left arm is extended upward it signals a right turn; be aware when following vehicles using hand signals.

question: How should you apply the gas pedal for smooth acceleration?
options: a:Gradually and smoothly.,b:By tapping rapidly for quick bursts.,c:As quickly as possible to merge with traffic.
note: Accelerate gradually and smoothly with the ball of your foot on the pedal and your heel on the floor to maintain control.

question: Under what circumstances may you drink alcoholic beverages in a vehicle on a public highway?
options: a:As long as you are not the driver.,b:Never; it is illegal to consume or possess an open container in the passenger area.,c:If you are riding in the back seat.,d:If you are riding in the back of a pickup truck.
note: It is unlawful on public roads to consume or possess an open alcoholic beverage in the passenger area of a motor vehicle; storing an open container in areas normally occupied by driver or passengers is prohibited.

question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is nearby while you are driving, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to avoid it.,b:Stop immediately and block its path.,c:Make every effort to give it a clear path of travel (pull over if safe).
note: If safe, pull to the side and yield to emergency vehicles so they can pass or reach their destination quickly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see a Merging traffic sign on the freeway, what should you do if traffic is present beside you?
options: a:Always remain at your present speed.,b:Honk at incoming traffic.,c:Make room for entering vehicles if possible.
note: When safe, move over or adjust your speed to make room for merging traffic; if no vehicle is beside you, you may move over a lane.

question: Does the type of alcoholic beverage determine how much it impairs you?
options: a:Beer is less impairing than wine.,b:Effects depend on the amount of alcohol in your bloodstream, not the beverage type.,c:Hard ciders and mixed drinks are most impairing.
note: Impairment depends on the amount of alcohol consumed and blood alcohol concentration, not the specific type of beverage.

question: If you approach a railroad crossing and you neither see nor hear a train, when must you stop?
options: a:If a stop sign is posted.,b:If a crossing gate is lowered.,c:If the crossing lights are flashing.
note: Stop at railroad crossings when a stop sign is posted, lights are flashing, a gate is lowered, a flagger signals, or a train is visible or close enough to be hazardous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you have the right-of-way at an intersection, you should:
options: a:Assume other drivers will obey right-of-way rules and proceed without looking.,b:Take extra time to check for crossing traffic and bicyclists before moving.,c:Wave other drivers forward before proceeding.,d:Immediately accelerate through the intersection.
note: Even with the right-of-way, always check for other vehicles and pedestrians before entering an intersection to avoid collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it safe to pass another vehicle?
options: a:When the centerline on your side is a broken yellow line and it is safe to do so.,b:When in a curve or on a hill because you are unlikely to meet oncoming traffic.,c:By using the shoulder of the roadway.
note: You may pass only where the markings permit (for example, a broken yellow on your side) and when it is safe to do so; never pass on curves, hills, or by using the shoulder.

question: Two solid white lines painted across a traffic lane mark what and how should drivers respond?
options: a:They mark a bike lane and drivers have priority.,b:They show crosswalk boundaries; yield to pedestrians in crosswalks.,c:They indicate no one has right-of-way.
note: Crosswalk markings show where pedestrians cross; drivers must stop for and yield to pedestrians in crosswalks.

question: To cross railroad tracks safely, what should you do?
options: a:Look both ways only when the red light is flashing.,b:Listen, look both ways, and then proceed if it is safe to do so.,c:Cross quickly when a train is approaching.,d:Rely on other drivers to signal whether it is safe.
note: Always listen and look for approaching trains from both directions; watch for warning signals and do not cross until you are sure it is safe.

question: Which of the following is a telltale sign of a drunk driver?
options: a:Driving more slowly than the normal traffic flow.,b:Weaving between lanes.,c:Making quick and sudden stops.,d:Driving with headlights off.
note: Common signs of impaired driving include weaving, speeding or driving too slowly, jerking motions, and sudden stops.

question: Crossbuck signs indicate:
options: a:Railroad crossings.,b:School zones.,c:No passing zones.,d:Pedestrian crossings.
note: Crossbuck signs mark railroad crossings and indicate drivers must yield to any approaching trains.

question: Regulatory signs are used to:
options: a:Warn about possible hazards.,b:Provide directions to cities and towns.,c:Indicate what a driver must or must not do.,d:Give distance to the next exit.
note: Regulatory signs inform drivers of traffic laws and requirements — what they must or must not do (speed limits, turn prohibitions, etc.).

question: When driving at night and another vehicle is approaching, which headlight setting should you use?
options: a:High beams.,b:Low beams.,c:Parking lights only.
note: Do not use high beams when approaching or following another vehicle; use low beams to avoid blinding others.

question: It is best to keep a space cushion:
options: a:Only behind your vehicle.,b:Only on the left and right sides of your vehicle.,c:Only in front of your vehicle.,d:On all sides of your vehicle.
note: Maintain a cushion of space around your vehicle — front, rear, and sides — to give yourself time and space to react to hazards.

question: You may pass another vehicle when the line dividing your lane from the lane you wish to enter is which type of line?
options: a:Double solid yellow,line not crossable.,b:Broken white,line that separates lanes traveling in same direction.,c:Solid yellow,line you must not cross.,d:Broken yellow,line dividing opposing traffic.
note: White lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction; a broken white line may be crossed to pass when it is safe to do so.

question: Approximately how far might a fully loaded tractor-trailer need to stop from 55 mph?
options: a:125 feet,b:50 feet,c:400 feet.
note: Large tractor-trailers require much longer distances to stop than passenger cars; a fully loaded truck at 55 mph can take up to about 400 feet to stop.

question: A traffic light showing a green arrow with a red light means:
options: a:You may go straight in any direction.,b:You may only move in the direction the green arrow indicates and only if the way is clear.,c:You must wait for a solid green light to go in that direction.,d:You may turn left without yielding to pedestrians.
note: A green arrow gives you permission to move only in the arrow’s direction; yield to pedestrians and ensure the intersection is clear before proceeding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you reach an intersection and are not in the proper lane to turn, what should you do?
options: a:Turn on your blinker and make the turn from your current lane.,b:Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.,c:Drive to the next intersection and make the turn from the proper lane.
note: Do not make last-minute turns or cut across traffic; continue to the next intersection and turn from the correct lane.

question: Traffic signs and pavement markings:
options: a:Must always be obeyed.,b:Are merely suggestions.,c:Must be followed only when other traffic is present.,d:Apply only to commercial vehicles.
note: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings control traffic and must be obeyed to ensure safety and order on the road.

question: Which statement about yielding to emergency vehicles is correct?
