options: a:May follow each other.,b:May use a loudspeaker to give instructions.,c:Have the right-of-way when using sirens, horns, and/or flashing lights.
note: You must yield the right-of-way to emergency vehicles using sirens or flashing lights and follow any instructions given by their loudspeakers.

question: When a vehicle with Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) starts to lose traction, drivers should:
options: a:Pump the brakes manually.,b:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly and steer out of danger.,c:Release the brake immediately.,d:Shift to neutral and coast.
note: With ABS, press and hold the brake firmly while steering to avoid the hazard; ABS will automatically modulate braking for you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on a freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Make the turn quickly from your lane of travel.,b:Stop and back up.,c:Continue to the next exit or safe location to turn around.
note: If you miss an exit, continue on to the next exit; never stop or back up on the freeway or shoulder.

question: How does increasing speed affect your field of vision?
options: a:It increases your field of vision.,b:It decreases your field of vision.,c:It makes it easier to see cross traffic.
note: As speed increases your field of vision narrows, reducing your ability to see and react to hazards.

question: Traffic may NOT pass from either direction over which centerline marking?
options: a:A single broken yellow line.,b:A combination solid and broken yellow line.,c:Double solid yellow lines.
note: Double solid yellow lines indicate no passing for traffic in either direction.

question: What should you do when approaching a flashing yellow traffic signal?
options: a:Increase your speed.,b:Come to a complete stop.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow light warns of a hazard; slow down and proceed carefully.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do when you reach an intersection controlled by a flashing red light?
options: a:Stop and wait for a flashing green light.,b:Come to a full stop and proceed only when the way is clear.,c:Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.,d:Yield to oncoming traffic but do not stop.
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop. Proceed only when it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If your vehicle's turn signals fail, you should use which method to indicate turns?
options: a:Your horn.,b:Your headlights.,c:Hand signals.,d:Tail lights only.
note: If turn signals are not functioning, use standard hand signals to indicate your intention to turn or stop until you can repair the signals.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What moves are allowed from a center lane marked for two-way left turns?
options: a:You may pass slow-moving traffic.,b:You may make left turns.,c:You may make U-turns.
note: A center two-way left-turn lane is for left turns (and legal U-turns where permitted), not for passing or through travel.

question: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) depends on each of the following except:
options: a:How much you drink.,b:How much time passes between drinks.,c:Your body weight.,d:The type of alcoholic beverage you drink.
note: BAC is affected by the amount of alcohol consumed, the time over which it is consumed, and body weight. The type of beverage (beer, wine, liquor) does not determine BAC by itself.

question: How should head restraints be positioned for safety?
options: a:Removed from the seats if possible.,b:Adjusted to contact the back of the head.,c:Adjusted to sit above the head.
note: Head restraints should be positioned to contact the back of the head to help reduce whiplash injuries in a collision.

question: If you are involved in an accident, which of the following actions should you take at the scene?
options: a:Stop your vehicle at or near the scene.,b:Turn off the ignitions of wrecked vehicles.,c:Avoid standing in traffic lanes.
note: Stop at or near the scene, move your vehicle out of traffic if possible, turn off ignitions of wrecked vehicles, and avoid standing in lanes of traffic.

question: If you hit an unattended parked vehicle and cannot find the owner, you must:
options: a:Leave a note with your name, address, and the circumstances of the accident.,b:Drive away if damage appears minor.,c:Wait until the police arrive before leaving any information.,d:Do nothing unless someone witnessed the accident.
note: If you damage an unattended vehicle, leave a written note with your name, address, and details of the incident, and report it to authorities if required.

question: If nearby drivers are reacting angrily, what should you do?
options: a:Do not make eye contact and avoid gestures.,b:Try to engage with them to resolve the issue.,c:Speed up to get away from them quickly.
note: Avoid eye contact and provocative gestures, and distance yourself from angry drivers by slowing, changing lanes, or pulling over when safe.

question: What is the purpose of highway pavement markings?
options: a:They are usually not important.,b:They are only used in construction zones.,c:They provide information and guidance to drivers.
note: Pavement markings guide drivers on lane positioning, passing zones, and upcoming roadway conditions—obey them for safety.

question: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder, what is the safest way to return to the road?
options: a:Slow down and very carefully turn back onto the pavement.,b:Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the pavement.,c:Stop your car on the edge of the road.,d:Accelerate back onto the pavement immediately.
note: If your wheels drop onto a low shoulder, reduce speed without braking sharply and carefully steer back onto the pavement when safe.

question: If a tire blows out while driving, you should:
options: a:Brake hard immediately.,b:Maintain speed and steer straight.,c:Hold the wheel firmly and gradually slow by easing off the gas.
note: If a tire blows out, keep the vehicle straight, ease off the gas, do not brake hard until you have control, then slow and pull off the road safely.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing, which action should you take?
options: a:Cross especially quickly when a train is approaching.,b:Look for a train.,c:Slow down only if lights are flashing.,d:Ignore warning gates and continue.
note: When you approach any railroad crossing, look and listen for trains and be prepared to stop; if warning lights flash or gates are down, stop and remain stopped.

question: What plates are required on Colorado motor vehicles?
options: a:A plate only on the rear.,b:Plates on both the front and back of the vehicle.,c:A plate only on the front.
note: Colorado requires license plates be displayed on both the front and rear of most motor vehicles.

question: Which statement about work zones is true?
options: a:May be moving or stationary.,b:Is marked with black and white signs.,c:Does not require a driver to slow down and pay extra attention.
note: Work zones can be stationary or moving (e.g., road crews, striping machines) and are typically marked with orange signs; slow down and pay close attention.

question: A slow-moving vehicle emblem is:
options: a:A circular green sign.,b:A diamond-shaped yellow sign.,c:A reflective orange triangle.,d:A rectangular red sign.
note: The slow-moving vehicle emblem is a reflective orange triangle indicating a vehicle traveling 25 mph or slower; approach with caution.

question: If the driver behind you wants to pass, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to prevent the pass.,b:Go the same speed.,c:Slow down to give room in front of your vehicle for the pass.
note: Slow down to create space in front of your vehicle so the other driver can pass safely.

question: What color pavement markings separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions?
options: a:Yellow,b:White,c:Both yellow and white
note: Yellow pavement markings are used to separate traffic moving in opposite directions; white separates same-direction lanes.

question: Which statement is true about alcohol and driving skills?
options: a:Only a BAC above the legal limit will impair concentration and judgment.,b:Alcohol does not affect driving.,c:Even the smallest amount of alcohol can impair concentration, perception, judgment, and memory.
note: Even small amounts of alcohol reduce concentration and judgment; no amount of drinking is safe when driving.

question: What should your inside rearview mirror show after adjustment?
options: a:The passengers in the backseat.,b:Your own reflection.,c:The entire rear window.
note: Adjust the inside rearview mirror so from the driver’s seat you can see the entire rear window without moving your head.

question: When driving near a motorcycle, you must:
options: a:Allow the motorcycle to use a complete lane.,b:Allow the motorcycle to use only half a lane.,c:Drive on the shoulder beside the motorcycle.
note: A motorcycle is a full-size vehicle and must be given a full lane width for safe operation; do not try to share their lane space.

question: Which of these is a common effect of alcohol on a driver?
options: a:Improved judgment.,b:Poor coordination.,c:Increased alertness.
note: Alcohol impairs coordination, judgment, concentration, vision, and reaction time—even small amounts can be dangerous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a right turn, your vehicle should be positioned:
options: a:Near the center of the street.,b:Close to the left side of the street.,c:As close as possible to the right side of the street.,d:In the middle of the intersection.
note: Prepare for a right turn by getting as far to the right side of the roadway as is safe and legal.

question: What does a red and white triangular sign at an intersection indicate?
options: a:Always come to a full stop at the intersection.,b:Yield to vehicles or pedestrians in the intersection.,c:Slow down if an emergency vehicle is approaching.
note: A red-and-white triangular sign is a yield sign: slow down and yield the right-of-way to vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection.

question: If another driver behaves aggressively toward you, what should you do?
options: a:Retaliate by tailgating them.,b:Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.,c:Cut them off to slow them down.
note: Remain calm, avoid eye contact or gestures, slow down, and allow aggressive drivers to pass to reduce the risk of escalation.

question: Why is maintaining a space cushion around your vehicle important?
options: a:It prevents distractions from other vehicles.,b:It gives you time to react to unexpected situations.,c:It helps keep traffic speed consistent.
note: A space cushion gives you time and space to react to mistakes or sudden actions by other road users.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on an interstate, what should you do?
options: a:Stop and make a U-turn.,b:Get off at the next exit and come back safely.,c:Back up on the shoulder to return to the exit.
note: If you miss an exit, continue to the next exit and re-route — never back up or make a U-turn on the highway.

question: If you become stranded in a snowstorm, the best action is to:
options: a:Get out of the car and walk for help.,b:Stay in your car and wait for help.,c:Lay down in your car and sleep.,d:Walk into the road to attract passing motorists.
note: If stranded in a snowstorm, remain in your vehicle where you are most likely to be found, conserve heat, and call for help if possible.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must not pass:
options: a:On a hill or curve where your view is blocked.,b:When a school bus has flashing red lights and is stopped to load/unload (unless separated by a median).,c:When approaching an intersection.,d:All of the above.
note: Passing is prohibited where you cannot see far enough ahead (hills/curves), at intersections, and generally when a school bus has activated its flashing red lights unless divided roadways separate traffic.

question: Roads tend to become very slippery:
options: a:When it has been raining for an hour or more.,b:Only after several days of rain.,c:During the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.,d:When the temperature is above 100°F.
note: Pavement can be especially slick in the first 10–15 minutes of rain as oils on the surface mix with water; reduce speed and increase following distance.

question: What is the safest way to pass a bicyclist?
options: a:Slow down and give the bicyclist as much room as possible.,b:Honk at the bicyclist to alert them.,c:Drive in the bicycle lane until you can pass.
note: When passing a bicyclist, slow down and give plenty of space; do not pass too quickly or too close since bicyclists have little protection.

question: Which of the following is NOT a factor in determining your vehicle's stopping distance?
options: a:Steering ability.,b:Braking distance.,c:Reaction distance.,d:Perception time.
note: Stopping distance depends on perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance; steering ability is not a primary factor in the stopping distance calculation.

question: What are the consequences for parking illegally in a space designated for disabled drivers?
options: a:No negative consequences.,b:Only a small fine.,c:Fines and possible jail time and other penalties.
note: Illegally parking in a designated accessible space can result in large fines, possible jail time, loss of privileges, and impoundment.

question: You must stop at an intersection when you see which signal?
options: a:A steady yellow light.,b:A yellow arrow.,c:A flashing red light.
note: A flashing red traffic signal has the same meaning as a stop sign: come to a complete stop, then proceed when it is safe.

question: A single dashed yellow line separating two directions of traffic means:
options: a:Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.,b:Both lanes travel in the same direction.,c:Drivers may not pass.,d:A turn lane is ahead.
note: A dashed yellow centerline permits passing when it is safe and legal to do so; exercise caution before initiating a pass.

question: If you are waiting to turn left and opposing traffic blocks your view, what should you do?
options: a:Accelerate rapidly when the first lane is clear.,b:Wait until you can see all the lanes you must cross before making the turn.,c:Wait for an oncoming driver to wave you across.
note: Do not start a left turn until you can see that all lanes you need to cross are clear and you can complete the turn safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic light changes from green to yellow as you approach, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to beat the light.,b:Be prepared to stop if it is safe to do so.,c:Stop in the center of the intersection.
note: A steady yellow warns the light will soon turn red; slow and prepare to stop unless you are already too close to stop safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles arrive at an intersection at the same time and there are no signs or signals, which vehicle has the right-of-way?
options: a:The car approaching from the left has the right-of-way.,b:The car approaching from the right has the right-of-way.,c:The car whose driver sounds the horn first has the right-of-way.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection, yield to the vehicle approaching from your right when you both arrive simultaneously.

question: If you must drive in fog, what should you do with your lights?
options: a:Turn on your hazard lights.,b:Turn on your parking lights.,c:Turn on your low beam headlights.
note: Use low beam headlights (and fog lights if equipped) in fog; high beams reduce visibility by reflecting off the fog.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left you must yield the right-of-way to which road users?
options: a:Drivers already in the intersection only.,b:Oncoming traffic and any pedestrians in the intersection.,c:Vehicles behind you that started moving last.
note: When turning left yield to oncoming traffic and to pedestrians and bicyclists who are already in the intersection.

question: If you are involved in a crash and your vehicle is blocking traffic, what should you do if possible?
options: a:Move your vehicle off the traveled portion of the roadway.,b:Never move your vehicle under any circumstances.,c:Wait for police before moving anything.
note: After a minor collision, move the vehicle off the roadway if it can be done safely; do not leave the scene and render aid if needed.

question: What is the most common color used for general warning signs?
options: a:Red.,b:Yellow.,c:Green.
note: Most warning signs are diamond-shaped and yellow with black symbols; they warn of unexpected conditions ahead.

question: What does a single broken yellow center line indicate on a two-lane road?
options: a:Lanes move in opposite directions; passing is allowed when safe.,b:Lanes move in opposite directions; passing is never allowed.,c:Lanes move in the same direction and passing is not allowed.
note: A single broken yellow line separates opposite directions of traffic; drivers may pass when it is safe to do so.

question: To help ensure your physical condition does not impair your driving, you should:
options: a:Know how any medication affects your ability to drive.,b:Keep physically fit and have regular medical check-ups.,c:Drive within your physical limitations.,d:All of the above.
note: Drivers should be aware of their health, medications, and limitations; take steps such as regular check-ups and avoid driving when impaired by illness or medication.

question: What does a flashing red light on a traffic signal indicate?
options: a:The traffic signal is broken.,b:The same thing as a stop sign.,c:You do not have to come to a complete stop.
note: A flashing red light functions like a stop sign: drivers must stop, yield, and only proceed when safe.

question: When may you park or stop along the shoulder of a freeway?
options: a:If you need to look at a map for directions.,b:Only in an emergency.,c:As long as you turn on your four-way (emergency) flashers.,d:If no part of your vehicle is on the road.
note: Parking on the shoulder of a freeway is prohibited except in an emergency. If you must stop, use your emergency flashers and call for assistance if needed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may a driver text while driving?
options: a:Only in an emergency.,b:At any time if the driver is 18 or older.,c:If the driver can send a text without looking at the phone.
note: Texting while driving is prohibited except for emergency calls; looking away from the road to text greatly increases crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From which lane should you start a left turn on multilane one-way streets or highways?
options: a:The middle of the intersection.,b:The left lane.,c:The right lane.
note: When turning left from multilane one-way streets or highways, begin the turn from the leftmost lane.

question: Which road areas tend to freeze first in cold or wet weather?
options: a:Roads in the sun.,b:Shaded sections of the road.,c:Flat open areas.
note: Shaded parts of the road (under trees or buildings) freeze sooner and dry later than exposed areas.

question: What color lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction?
options: a:White.,b:Yellow.,c:Red.
note: White lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction; yellow lines separate opposite directions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a stop is required at an intersection with no stop line or crosswalk, where should you stop?
options: a:Stop at the nearest point where you can see approaching traffic without entering the intersection.,b:You are not required to stop.,c:Always stop only after entering the intersection to get a better view.
note: If there are no stop markings, stop at the point nearest the intersecting roadway where you can see approaching traffic without entering the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a street from a driveway, what must you do?
options: a:Drive slowly to allow approaching vehicles and pedestrians time to get out of your way.,b:Must honk your horn so approaching vehicles and pedestrians know to give you room.,c:Stop and proceed only when there are no pedestrians or vehicles approaching.
note: Always stop before entering the roadway from a driveway, yield to approaching traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when safe.

question: When roads are slippery, what adjustment should you make?
options: a:Drive the same as on dry roads.,b:Increase your following distance.,c:Use alternate routes only.
note: On slippery roads you should increase following distance because stopping distances are longer.

question: How should you react when you are behind a transit bus signaling to re-enter a traffic lane?
options: a:Quickly pass the bus before it merges.,b:Yield the right-of-way and allow the bus to re-enter.,c:Expect the bus to yield to you.
note: Yield to the bus by changing lanes or slowing to allow it to merge safely back into traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver entering interstate traffic from an entrance ramp should do what?
options: a:Force their way into traffic.,b:Yield to drivers already on the interstate.,c:Stop at the ramp until a gap appears.
note: When merging from an entrance ramp, yield to vehicles already on the interstate and merge safely into traffic.

question: In which situations is it especially important to slow down?
options: a:On narrow or winding roads.,b:At intersections or railroad crossings.,c:When the road is wet or slippery.,d:All of the above.
note: Reduce speed on narrow or winding roads, at intersections and railroad crossings, and when roads are wet or otherwise hazardous.

question: What does an 'End school zone' sign mean?
options: a:The end of a reduced school zone speed limit.,b:The beginning of a reduced school speed zone.,c:An increased possibility of encountering pedestrians ahead.
note: An 'End school zone' sign indicates you are leaving the reduced school speed zone and normal speed limits apply beyond the sign.

question: A sign that reads 'Reduced speed, 35 mph' indicates what?
options: a:The new 35 mph speed limit begins at this sign.,b:You have plenty of time to slow down before the reduced zone.,c:The new 35 mph speed limit begins at the next speed limit sign.
note: A posted reduced speed sign indicates the new posted speed begins at the location of that sign; slow to the posted speed at that point.

question: Which of these is an effect alcohol can have on drivers?
options: a:It impairs your thinking ability.,b:It slows your reaction time.,c:It gives you a feeling of false confidence.
note: Alcohol impairs judgment and thinking, slows reaction time, and often produces a false sense of confidence — all of which affect driving.

question: Which actions help prevent hydroplaning?
options: a:Reduce speed when driving in the rain.,b:Ensure tires are properly inflated.,c:Ensure tires have good tread depth.
note: To reduce the risk of hydroplaning, slow down in wet conditions and make sure your tires are properly inflated with adequate tread.

question: What does a double solid yellow line down the center of a two-lane road indicate?
options: a:Lanes moving in opposite directions and passing is not allowed.,b:Lanes moving in opposite directions and passing is allowed anytime.,c:Lanes moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate opposing traffic and prohibit passing for vehicles in either direction.

question: How can you help avoid drowsiness on long trips?
options: a:Keep the radio on loudly.,b:Slow down your speed.,c:Stop regularly to rest and stretch.
note: Take regular stops to rest and stretch to reduce drowsiness on long drives.

question: When the center of the road has a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line with the broken line next to your lane, when may you pass?
options: a:Only in an emergency.,b:If you are on an expressway.,c:If traffic is clear.,d:Never.
note: If the broken yellow line is next to your lane, you may cross it to pass when it is safe and no oncoming traffic is present.

question: When is it appropriate to sound your horn?
options: a:When you have to stop quickly.,b:When passing another car.,c:If you have lost control of your vehicle and need to warn others.
note: Use your horn to warn other road users of immediate danger, such as losing control; do not use it aggressively or unnecessarily.

question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
options: a:New drivers,b:Human error,c:Bad weather,d:Vehicle defects
note: Most crashes result from human error — mistakes in perception, judgment, or vehicle control — more than from weather or vehicle problems.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you use your turn signals?
options: a:Changing lanes.,b:Pulling into or out of a parking space.,c:Pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.
note: You should signal whenever you change direction or lanes, including when pulling into traffic or into/out of a parking space.

question: At dusk or on overcast days, what should you do about your vehicle lights?
options: a:Turn on your headlights.,b:Drive using your four-way flashers.,c:Use only your parking lights.
note: Turn on your headlights at dusk or during overcast daylight when visibility is reduced; use low beams near other vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are stopped in line at a stop sign and the cross traffic is clear after cars ahead pass, what must you do?
options: a:May proceed through the intersection without stopping again.,b:Must stop again at the stop sign or stop line before proceeding.,c:May slowly roll past the stop sign.
note: You must come to a complete stop at the stop sign or stop line each time before proceeding, even if traffic ahead has already cleared the intersection.

question: Drivers should be extra alert to motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians because:
options: a:They always have the right-of-way.,b:They obey different traffic laws than motor vehicles.,c:They can be more difficult to see in traffic.,d:They are always traveling at the same speed as traffic.
note: Smaller road users can be harder to see due to size and less noticeable lighting; scan carefully and give them space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you turn onto a two-lane road divided by a broken yellow center line, what does that tell you?
options: a:The road is under repair.,b:You are on a one-way road.,c:You are on a two-way road.
note: Broken yellow centerlines separate traffic moving in opposite directions; you may cross them to pass when it is safe.

question: What is the effect of eating or drinking while driving?
options: a:It eliminates the need for seat belts.,b:It can cause distraction and lead to driving errors.,c:It makes you a better driver because you are not hungry.
note: Eating or drinking while driving distracts you by taking hands off the wheel and eyes off the road, increasing the risk of lane deviation and collisions.

question: What is a \No zone\"?"
options: a:A designated no passing zone.,b:A one-way traffic area.,c:The large blind spots around a truck or other large vehicle.,d:A restricted parking area.
note: A \No zone\" refers to the large blind spots around trucks and buses where the truck driver may not see other vehicles; avoid lingering there."

question: What is one effective way to avoid needing to make an emergency stop in traffic?
options: a:Honk your horn frequently.,b:Look ahead and keep a safe following distance.,c:Drive only in the right lane.
note: Maintaining a safe following distance and scanning ahead lets you react to hazards gradually and avoid sudden stops.

question: If you are being tailgated and there is no right lane, what should you do?
options: a:Brake suddenly to get them to back off.,b:Wait until the way ahead is clear and gently reduce your speed to encourage them to pass.,c:Speed up to create more distance.
note: If you cannot move right, wait for a clear stretch and then gently reduce speed so the tailgater can pass; never brake abruptly.

question: Is it ever permissible to drive around or under a lowering or raising railroad crossing gate?
options: a:Only if you can do so without damaging the gate.,b:If an approaching train is not too close.,c:No — you must not go around or under the gate while it is moving.
note: Never drive around or under a crossing gate; wait until signals stop and gates are fully raised before crossing.

question: Before backing out of a driveway with children nearby, what should you do?
options: a:Sound your horn so the children will hear you.,b:Rev your engine to warn the children that you are moving.,c:Walk to the back of the car to be sure the way is clear.
note: When children are nearby, get out of the vehicle and check behind it before backing up rather than relying solely on mirrors or sensors.

question: The effect that lack of sleep has on driving ability is most similar to the effect of which substance?
options: a:The effect that alcohol has.,b:The effect that amphetamines have.,c:The effect that anger has.,d:The effect that high caffeine intake has.
note: Fatigue impairs driving in ways similar to alcohol; for example, 18 hours awake can impair driving similar to a BAC of 0.05%.

question: If an emergency vehicle using flashing lights approaches while you are on a one-way street, what must you do?
options: a:Drive with your flashers turned on.,b:Drive toward the nearest roadside and stop.,c:Speed up and take the nearest exit.
note: On a one-way street, pull to the nearest roadside and stop to yield for an approaching emergency vehicle using lights or siren.

question: What do double solid yellow lines down the center of the road indicate?
options: a:Passing is not permitted from either direction.,b:Pedestrian crossing ahead.,c:Railroad crossing ahead.
note: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing from either direction except when turning into a driveway or making a permitted left turn.

question: To check your blind spot when changing lanes to the left, you should glance:
options: a:Over your right shoulder.,b:At your side mirror.,c:Over your left shoulder.
note: To check a left-lane blind spot, glance over your left shoulder in the direction you plan to move.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing with only a crossbuck and no gates or lights, how should you proceed?
options: a:Turn down your radio to listen for a train.,b:Proceed only after you are certain no train is coming.,c:Only continue once a flagger clears you to do so.
note: Approach such crossings with extreme caution and cross only when you know no train is coming from either direction.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing warning sign you should:
options: a:Be ready to drive faster than the train.,b:Be prepared to stop if a train is nearby.,c:Look for a way around any lowered gates.,d:Speed up to cross before the train arrives.
note: Railroad crossing warning signs indicate you may need to stop; always slow and be prepared to stop when a train is approaching.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, you should:
options: a:Continue to the next exit and re-enter the freeway to reach your destination.,b:Make a U-turn through the median.,c:Pull onto the shoulder and back up to the exit.,d:Stop on the freeway and reverse to the exit.
note: If you miss an exit, proceed to the next exit — do not stop, back up, or attempt unsafe maneuvers on the freeway.

question: A broken yellow line beside a solid yellow line means:
options: a:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the broken line but not from the lane next to the solid line.,b:Passing is permitted from either direction.,c:Passing from the lane next to the solid line is allowed.,d:Traffic moves in the same direction on both sides.
note: When a broken yellow line is next to a solid yellow line, vehicles next to the broken line may pass when safe; vehicles next to the solid line may not.

question: When riding in a vehicle, small children:
options: a:May be safely held by a strong adult in a crash.,b:Will be safe if standing on the floor in the back of the vehicle.,c:Will not be hurt in a crash because they are small.,d:Must be properly secured in an appropriate child restraint or safety seat.
note: Children must be placed in proper child restraints or safety seats suited to their age, height, and weight; holding a child in a crash is not safe.

question: Which factor greatly affects your ability to stop safely?
options: a:The condition of the road surface.,b:The time of day.,c:The color of your vehicle.
note: Your stopping distance is heavily affected by road conditions (wet, icy, gravel), which require reduced speed and increased following distance.

question: While driving uphill behind a heavy truck, what should you know about the truck's speed?
options: a:You may not be able to legally pass the truck.,b:The truck may be traveling at a speed slower than the posted speed limit.,c:You may not be able to safely pass the truck.
note: Large trucks often travel more slowly uphill; exercise caution when approaching and avoid attempting unsafe passes on hills.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a traffic signal turns solid yellow as you approach, what should you do?
options: a:Stop before entering the intersection unless you are too close to stop safely.,b:Consider it the same as a caution sign and speed up through the intersection.,c:Stop immediately wherever you are.
note: On a change to solid yellow, slow and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely; proceed if you are too close to stop safely.

question: What does checking your blind spot by turning your head before changing lanes represent?
options: a:A bad driving habit.,b:A good driving habit.,c:An unnecessary action.
note: Turning your head to check blind spots is a good habit and necessary for safe lane changes.

question: Your first response to reduced visibility should be to:
options: a:Turn on your headlights.,b:Reduce your speed.,c:Turn on your windshield wipers.,d:Increase cabin lighting.
note: When visibility decreases, slow down first so you have more time to react; use headlights and wipers as appropriate.

question: If a green arrow changes to a solid green light, you:
options: a:Retain an automatic right-of-way to turn with no yielding.,b:May still turn in the arrow’s direction but must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,c:May no longer turn and must go straight.,d:Must wait for a flashing yellow before turning.
note: When a green arrow ends and a green light appears, you may still make the turn but must yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.

question: What is a blind spot?
options: a:An area you cannot see without moving your head.,b:A place directly behind your vehicle.,c:An area you can see in your rearview mirror.
note: Blind spots are areas to the sides or rear of your vehicle that you cannot see without turning your head to check.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you meet an oncoming vehicle on a narrow road, what must you allow?
options: a:Demand the other vehicle pull over to make room.,b:Allow the oncoming vehicle at least one-half of the main-traveled portion of the road.,c:Pull completely off the road and stop.,d:Speed up and pass quickly.
note: On narrow roads, each vehicle must allow the other at least one-half of the main-traveled portion of the road so both can pass safely.

question: Anything that causes you to do which of the following could lead to a crash?
options: a:Take your eyes off the road.,b:Take your hands off the wheel.,c:Take your attention away from driving.,d:Any of the above.
note: Distractions that take your eyes, hands, or attention away from driving increase the risk of a crash.

question: When driving in fog, which lights should you use?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Parking lights.,c:Low beam headlights.
note: Use low beam headlights (and fog lights if equipped) in fog. High beams reflect off fog and reduce visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway, it is usually best to:
options: a:Proceed slowly while waiting for an opening.,b:Use the on-ramp to accelerate to the speed of freeway traffic and merge when safe.,c:Turn on your hazard lights until you are fully on the freeway.,d:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a large gap.
note: Use the acceleration lane to match the speed of traffic and merge smoothly; vehicles on the freeway have the right-of-way.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A speed limit sign indicates what?
options: a:The suggested speed to travel on a road under ideal conditions.,b:The maximum or minimum legal speed you can travel on a road under ideal conditions.,c:The maximum or minimum legal speed you can travel on a road under dangerous conditions.,d:The minimum safe speed at all times.
note: A posted speed limit indicates the maximum (or minimum) legal speed under ideal conditions; you must drive slower when conditions are hazardous.

question: Which driving technique helps avoid crashes on icy or snow-covered roads?
options: a:Engage four-wheel drive on your vehicle.,b:Reduce your speed and increase your following distance.,c:Add extra weight to your vehicle to improve traction.,d:Get off the highways as quickly as possible.
note: The primary techniques for safe winter driving are reducing speed and increasing following distance; four-wheel drive helps in some situations but is not a substitute for cautious driving.

question: When driving on major highways, what practices help avoid 'highway hypnosis'?
options: a:Keep your eyes fixed on a distant point.,b:Stay alert and keep your eyes moving.,c:Drive without breaks until your destination.
note: Stay alert, keep your eyes moving, and take breaks when necessary to avoid zoning out on long highway stretches.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a steady yellow traffic light, how should you respond?
options: a:Speed up to avoid a red light.,b:Slow and stop unless you are already within the intersection.,c:Continue because you have the right-of-way.
note: A steady yellow indicates the light will soon turn red; stop if it is safe to do so unless you are already in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection where another vehicle arrives at the same time and is on your right, you should:
options: a:Speed up and get through the intersection.,b:Slow down and yield to the vehicle on your right.,c:Drive into the intersection and force the other vehicle to stop.
note: When two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection simultaneously, yield to the vehicle on your right.

question: Which effect does alcohol have on driving-related abilities?
options: a:Puts you to sleep.,b:Wakes you up.,c:Slows reflexes and reaction time.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that slows brain activity, reflexes, and reaction time, impairing driving skills.

question: Regulatory traffic signs are usually what color and must be obeyed?
options: a:White,b:Blue,c:Green
note: Regulatory signs (which control traffic) are generally white with black markings and must be obeyed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Signaling before turning, changing lanes, or leaving a curb:
options: a:Is necessary only if other traffic is present.,b:Is required by law and is a good driving habit.,c:Is necessary only during the maneuver itself.,d:Is optional on private roads.
note: You must signal your intentions in advance (at least 100 feet in many areas) to inform other road users and improve safety.

question: When you see a school crossing sign, how should you react?
options: a:Always sound your horn when children are present.,b:Always stop whether a stop sign is posted or not.,c:Watch for children and be prepared to stop.
note: Be alert for children at school crossings and be ready to stop. Always yield to pedestrians in or entering a crosswalk.

question: To reduce the effects of oncoming headlight glare at night, where should you look?
options: a:Straight ahead.,b:Toward the right side of the road ahead.,c:Over your shoulder.
note: If oncoming headlights are blinding, avert your gaze slightly to the right edge of the roadway and use the lane markings as a guide.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless otherwise posted, what is the speed limit on blind curves?
options: a:40 mph,b:20 mph,c:55 mph
note: Unless posted otherwise, the advisory speed on blind curves is typically 20 mph; always follow posted advisory speeds.

question: When should you look over your shoulder to check your blind spot?
options: a:When turning left or right.,b:Only when backing up.,c:Before changing lanes.,d:Before pulling toward or away from a curb.
note: Always look over your shoulder to check your blind spot whenever you change your vehicle's position — for example, when turning, changing lanes, or pulling toward or away from a curb.

question: What should you remember when driving on wet pavement?
options: a:That wet roads can cause hydroplaning.,b:To give yourself extra room when stopping.,c:That pavement is most slippery just after it starts to rain.
note: Wet roads can cause hydroplaning and are especially slick when rain first begins; increase stopping distance and slow down.

question: How should you position your wheels when parking uphill on a street with a curb?
options: a:Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.,b:Turn your front wheels slightly to the right.,c:Turn your front wheels sharply toward the curb.,d:Keep your front wheels straight ahead.
note: When parked facing uphill with a curb, turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb so the vehicle will roll away from traffic if it moves.

question: What do downward-facing triangular road signs indicate?
options: a:School zones.,b:Yield.,c:Construction zones.
note: Downward-pointing triangular signs indicate that drivers should yield the right-of-way.

question: For drivers 21 or older, at what blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is it illegal to drive?
options: a:0.05 percent.,b:0.08 percent.,c:0.02 percent.
note: In Colorado it is illegal for drivers age 21 or older to operate a vehicle with a BAC of 0.08% or higher.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a flagger directs traffic in a construction zone, you must:
options: a:Follow the directions given by the flagger.,b:Assume the flagger is mistaken and follow other vehicles.,c:Ignore the flagger and proceed as usual.
note: Always obey instructions from a flagger, posted signs, and law enforcement in work zones for safety and legal compliance.

question: What does an arrow painted on the pavement indicate?
options: a:Drivers in the proper lane must make the movement indicated by the arrow.,b:Drivers in the proper lane may make the movement if they choose.,c:Drivers must always come to a complete stop before making the movement.,d:Only applies when traffic signals are not working.
note: A pavement arrow in a lane indicates that drivers in that lane must make the movement shown by the arrow and follow any posted signs or signals.

question: When interacting with pedestrians, what must a driver do?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way even if the pedestrian is crossing illegally.,b:Make certain the pedestrian is aware of the vehicle.,c:Yield only when the pedestrian has the legal right-of-way.
note: Drivers must do everything possible to avoid striking a pedestrian and should yield the right-of-way to pedestrians even if they are not crossing legally.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You should always signal when:
options: a:Changing lanes.,b:Pulling into or out of a parking space.,c:Pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.,d:All of the above.
note: Use proper turn signals when changing lanes, entering traffic, or pulling into/out of parking to communicate your intentions to others.

question: Which factors influence how alcohol affects a person?
options: a:How much time passes between drinks.,b:The amount of food in the stomach.,c:The body weight of the individual.
note: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is influenced by how much you drink, how quickly you drink (time between drinks), your weight, and food in the stomach.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you want to turn left and oncoming traffic is heavy when the light is green, what is a safe choice?
options: a:Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.,b:Use the next intersection.,c:Wait at the crosswalk for traffic to clear.
note: If you cannot safely turn left because of heavy oncoming traffic, a safe option is to go through the intersection and use the next legal opportunity to turn.

question: If you see a driver in the vehicle ahead who appears distracted (e.g., driving with one hand while conversing), you should:
options: a:Give the vehicle extra space.,b:Assume they will correct their behavior.,c:Follow closely to observe them.,d:Try to signal them to drive differently.
note: Allow extra following distance and be prepared for unpredictable actions by drivers who appear distracted.

question: A green arrow signal displayed for turns means:
options: a:It is used only on one-way streets.,b:Has the same meaning as a circular green light, but traffic must turn in the direction indicated by the arrow.,c:Means you may proceed in any direction once clear.,d:Means you must wait for a circular green light as well.
note: A green arrow allows traffic to turn in the direction shown; it functions like a circular green but requires you to turn in the indicated direction.

question: Which statement about changing weather and driving is true?
options: a:A sudden change in weather requires you to change your driving.,b:Be particularly aware of vehicles coming up behind you in inclement weather.,c:You should slow down when driving in rain and fog.
note: If weather changes suddenly, adjust your driving (reduce speed, increase following distance) to match road and visibility conditions.

question: When may you drive around lowered railroad crossing gates?
options: a:When the train has passed.,b:Under no circumstances.,c:When the lights have stopped flashing.
note: Do not go around a lowered gate; you must stop when crossing signals indicate a train is approaching.

question: When driving in fog, you should:
options: a:Use your high beam headlights to penetrate the fog.,b:Drive cautiously at reduced speed and use your low beam headlights.,c:Open all windows and increase ventilation.,d:Drive at your normal speed if visibility seems sufficient.
note: Fog reduces visibility; drive slowly and use low beam headlights (not high beams) so you can see and be seen more effectively.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A posted speed limit sign indicates:
options: a:The maximum safe driving speed under ideal conditions.,b:Only a suggested speed to help traffic flow.,c:The exact speed required to avoid a ticket.
note: A posted speed limit indicates the maximum legal speed under ideal conditions; drivers must slow down when conditions are not ideal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer stops you, how should you behave while waiting for the officer to approach?
options: a:Get your paperwork ready before the officer reaches your car.,b:Stay in your vehicle with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer to approach you.,c:Unbuckle your seat belt and lower your window.,d:Immediately exit the vehicle to speak with the officer.
note: Keep your hands visible, remain in the vehicle unless asked to get out, and wait until the officer requests your driver license, registration, and insurance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are turning left onto a one-way street, you should complete the turn into:
options: a:The right lane of the one-way street.,b:The lane closest to your previous lane (leftmost lane possible),c:Either lane as long as it’s clear.,d:The farthest lane from your approach.
note: When turning left onto a one-way street, turn into the lane closest to the lane you came from — usually the leftmost lane — unless signs indicate otherwise.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you approach an uncontrolled intersection?
options: a:Maintain your speed and proceed.,b:Stop at the intersection, check in all directions, and proceed.,c:Yield to all other drivers.,d:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.
note: At an intersection without signs or signals, slow, be prepared to yield (especially to vehicles from the right), cover your brake, look left-right-left, and proceed only when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about speed is true?
options: a:Driving too slowly on some highways is not dangerous.,b:Speeding can kill.,c:Speeding is not dangerous if you are a skilled driver.
note: Higher speeds increase the severity and likelihood of crashes; speeding can be fatal and is dangerous regardless of perceived skill.

question: When must drivers yield to pedestrians in the roadway?
options: a:Only when the pedestrian is in a crosswalk.,b:Even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly.,c:Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road as the driver.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in the street, even if the pedestrian is careless or crossing against a signal.

question: When parallel parking between two cars, what is the first positioning step?
options: a:Turn your wheels to the left.,b:Turn your wheels to the right.,c:Pull up even with the car in front of the desired space.
note: After signaling and checking traffic, stop parallel to the vehicle in front of the space before beginning the backing maneuver into the spot.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop where two drivers arrive simultaneously, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on the left.,b:The driver on the right.,c:Either driver may proceed without stopping.
note: When two drivers arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, yield to the vehicle on your right.

question: A 'No stopping' sign allows stopping only under which condition?
options: a:Long enough to unload packages.,b:To avoid conflict with other traffic.,c:To discharge passengers.,d:To briefly park while running an errand.
note: A 'No stopping' sign means you may only stop to obey a traffic signal, to obey a police officer, or to prevent a conflict with other traffic.

question: What is the only effective way to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Drink coffee or take a cold shower.,b:Exercise.,c:Allow your body time to remove the alcohol.,d:Take an over-the-counter stimulant.
note: Only time allows the body to metabolize alcohol and reduce BAC. Coffee, exercise, or cold showers do not sober you or reduce BAC.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Who may use a High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) lane?
options: a:You if you are driving faster than traffic.,b:You if you are driving more slowly than traffic.,c:Vehicles that have more than one occupant.
note: HOV lanes are restricted to vehicles with the required number of occupants (commonly two or more); check posted rules and diamond markings.

question: How should you react to a flashing red light at an intersection?
options: a:Stop only if other cars are also approaching the intersection.,b:Come to a full stop and go when it is safe to do so.,c:Stop only if other cars are already within the intersection.
note: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign: stop, yield, then proceed when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before entering a roundabout, you must slow down and yield to:
options: a:Vehicles already in the roundabout.,b:Bicyclists and pedestrians in the roundabout.,c:Pedestrians and bicyclists as well as vehicles in the roundabout.,d:All of the above.
note: When approaching a roundabout, slow down and yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and any vehicles already circulating in the roundabout.

question: A steady yellow traffic light at an intersection means:
options: a:Go through the intersection quickly.,b:Yield to other cars only.,c:Slow down and prepare to stop as the light will soon turn red.,d:The light will immediately turn green.
note: A steady yellow warns that the light will change to red; slow and prepare to stop unless you cannot do so safely.

question: What driving habit helps conserve gasoline?
options: a:Sitting in the driveway with the engine running.,b:Accelerating quickly.,c:Slowing down gradually and anticipating traffic flow.
note: Avoid rapid acceleration and frequent hard braking; anticipate traffic to maintain smoother speeds and better fuel economy.

question: A flashing red traffic signal at an intersection is equivalent to what sign?
options: a:A yield sign.,b:A slow sign.,c:A stop sign.
note: A flashing red signal means you must come to a complete stop and then proceed when safe, like a stop sign.

question: If another driver cuts you off, what is the best response?
options: a:Flash your high beams at the other driver.,b:Pull next to them and yell.,c:Let it go and continue driving safely.
note: To avoid road rage and unsafe reactions, do not take it personally—let it go and maintain safe driving behavior.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is it illegal and unsafe to attempt to pass another vehicle?
options: a:On hills and curves.,b:At controlled intersections only.,c:In urban parking lots only.
note: Passing is prohibited and unsafe on hills, curves, intersections, and at railroad crossings.

question: Which is a safe practice on potentially slippery roads?
options: a:Always drive at the maximum posted speed.,b:Use cruise control to maintain a steady speed.,c:Slow down.
note: On slippery roads, slow down, avoid sudden changes in direction or speed, increase following distance, and do not use cruise control.

question: If an approaching driver fails to dim high beams, you should look:
options: a:Directly at the headlights to signal them.,b:Toward the left side of the road.,c:Toward the right side of the road.,d:Into the centerline of the road.
note: Glance toward the right edge of the road to avoid being temporarily blinded by an oncoming vehicle's high beams while maintaining lane position.

question: To drive safely at night, you should:
options: a:Increase your following distance.,b:Not drive if you are tired.,c:Make sure your headlights are working properly.,d:All of the above.
note: Night driving requires working headlights, extra following distance, and avoiding driving while fatigued to maintain safety.

question: How can you reduce the chance of causing a rear-end crash?
options: a:Avoid sudden stops.,b:Before stopping, check mirrors and blind spots.,c:Release the gas to let the vehicle slow before applying the brakes.,d:All of the above.
note: To help prevent rear-end collisions, avoid sudden stops, give following drivers warning by slowing early, check mirrors and blind spots before stopping, and apply brakes smoothly.

question: Seat belts are most effective when worn by:
options: a:Only the person driving the car.,b:Only passengers on long trips.,c:Only occupants on expressways.,d:All occupants of the vehicle.
note: Seat belts protect all occupants; everyone in the vehicle should wear a seat belt to reduce injury in a crash.

question: Railroad crossings should always be treated as:
options: a:Safe places to stop and wait.,b:Dangerous locations that require caution.,c:Safe locations to park a vehicle temporarily.
note: Railroad crossings are potentially dangerous; always look and listen for trains and obey crossing signals and gates.

question: When a traffic light turns green, what should you do first?
options: a:Back up slowly.,b:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians.,c:Accelerate as quickly as possible.
note: A green light permits you to go, but first yield to any pedestrians and traffic that remain in the intersection.

question: How should you approach railroad tracks when driving?
options: a:Speed up to cross the tracks before the gate is lowered.,b:Look, listen, slow down, and be prepared to stop.,c:Try to drive around a lowered gate.
note: When approaching railroad tracks, slow down, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop if signage or signals indicate an approaching train.

question: On a road without sidewalks, which side should a pedestrian walk on?
options: a:Same side of the road on which traffic is moving.,b:Side with the lightest traffic.,c:The side of the road facing oncoming traffic.
note: Pedestrians should walk on the side facing oncoming traffic so they can see approaching vehicles and drivers can see them.

question: How should you behave when approaching a blind pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog?
options: a:Take the right-of-way and proceed.,b:Slow down and be prepared to stop.,c:Proceed normally without changing speed.
note: When near a blind pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog, slow, yield the right-of-way, and be prepared to stop to avoid causing harm.

question: When you approach a stopped emergency vehicle with its lights flashing, what must you do?
options: a:Stay in your lane and continue at the same speed.,b:Slow down and, if possible, change lanes away from the stopped vehicle.,c:Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
note: If possible, change lanes to leave extra space for stopped emergency or roadside assistance vehicles; otherwise slow down and pass carefully.

question: If you plan to drink socially, what is a safe way to ensure you get home safely?
options: a:Drink coffee before driving.,b:Take a cold shower.,c:Ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.
note: Arrange a sober ride home; coffee or showers do not lower blood alcohol concentration or effects.

question: When driving in traffic, what is generally the safest approach to speed?
options: a:Drive faster than the flow of traffic.,b:Drive slower than the flow of traffic.,c:Drive with the flow of traffic within the posted limits.
note: It is safest to travel with the flow of traffic while obeying the posted speed limit and adjusting for conditions.

question: If you are involved in a serious motor vehicle crash, what should you do first?
options: a:Leave the scene if no one looks injured.,b:Stop your vehicle.,c:Only call the police if your vehicle is completely undamaged.
note: If involved in a crash you must stop. Call 911 if anyone is injured. Report crashes to law enforcement when there is injury, death, or substantial property damage.

question: How should drivers respond to a school bus stopped with its stop arm extended?
options: a:Come to a complete stop and wait to proceed.,b:Honk before passing the bus on its left.,c:Continue when you think most kids are done exiting.,d:Pass slowly without stopping.
note: When a school bus is stopped with its stop arm extended, you are required to stop and must not proceed until the stop arm is withdrawn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a right turn on a green light, what must you do?
options: a:Maintain your normal driving speed.,b:Stop and look for nearby police cars.,c:Yield to pedestrians.
note: Before turning right on green, yield to pedestrians and any other traffic that has the right-of-way in the intersection.

question: Where is it illegal to park?
options: a:On a hill.,b:In a parking lot.,c:On a marked crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
note: Do not park on crosswalks or in designated bicycle lanes; follow local parking rules and keep within 12 inches of the curb when parking on the street.

question: Why is a leaky exhaust system dangerous?
options: a:A loss of hearing.,b:Pollution.,c:Carbon monoxide poisoning.
note: A leaking exhaust can allow carbon monoxide to enter the passenger compartment, risking carbon monoxide poisoning; repair leaks promptly.

question: How should you secure loose objects in your vehicle?
options: a:Place them on the back seat.,b:Put them on the floor near the driver's seat.,c:Secure them so they cannot become hazards in a crash.
note: Secure loose items to prevent them from flying and causing injury or interfering with vehicle controls during sudden stops or collisions.

question: What do round warning signs most often indicate?
options: a:School zones.,b:Upcoming railroad crossings.,c:No passing zones.
note: Round signs are used to warn drivers of an upcoming railroad crossing and to use caution.

question: What can happen when alcohol is consumed with other drugs?
options: a:The combination can decrease the effects of both substances.,b:The combination can increase the effects of both the drugs and alcohol.,c:The combination helps cure illnesses faster.
note: Combining alcohol with other drugs can amplify impairment and produce dangerous interactions; it increases risk and unpredictability.

question: If you drive much slower than the flow of traffic on a two-lane road and cars are backing up, what should you do?
options: a:Continue at your slow speed regardless of following traffic.,b:Pull off the road when safe to let others pass.,c:Refuse to let following cars pass.
note: If your slow driving causes traffic to back up on a two-lane road, you should pull off the roadway and allow others to pass when it is safe.

question: Which traffic signal indicates you should slow down and proceed with caution?
options: a:A flashing yellow light.,b:A flashing red light.,c:A solid yellow light.
note: A flashing yellow light warns of a hazard; slow down and proceed with caution.

question: Where are stop lines painted on the pavement?
options: a:Next to churches and schools.,b:In curves and on hills.,c:At intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.
note: Stop lines are solid white lines painted across lanes at intersections and crosswalks to show where vehicles must stop.

question: What usually causes hydroplaning?
options: a:Driving too fast for wet conditions.,b:Excessive stops.,c:Sudden turns.
note: Hydroplaning occurs when tires cannot clear water at higher speeds and lose contact with the road surface.

question: If you hear a siren behind you while driving, what is the correct action?
options: a:Stop where you are.,b:Pull over to the right and stop.,c:Speed up to get out of the way.
note: When an emergency vehicle is approaching from behind with sirens or lights, safely pull to the right and stop to allow it to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it legal to pass another vehicle on the right?
options: a:If the other vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is an available lane on the right.,b:Even if it means driving off the pavement.,c:On a narrow bridge.
note: You may pass on the right when the vehicle ahead is making or waiting to make a left turn and there is room; never pass by driving off the roadway.

question: How does smoking or preparing to smoke while driving affect your ability to drive?
options: a:Does not affect driving abilities.,b:Helps maintain driver alertness.,c:Is a distracting activity.,d:Is required to stay awake.
note: Smoking and preparing to smoke can distract you by taking your hands off the wheel or your eyes off the road, increasing crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless otherwise posted, what is the maximum speed limit on open mountain highways in Colorado?
options: a:55 mph,b:40 mph,c:20 mph,d:65 mph
note: Unless a different speed is posted, the maximum speed on open mountain highways in Colorado is 40 mph.

question: As alcohol builds up in your blood, what happens to your driving ability?
options: a:Makes you feel less confident.,b:Slows down your reactions.,c:Begins to metabolize itself more quickly.
note: Alcohol impairs judgment, slows reaction time, reduces coordination, and can give a false sense of confidence — impairing driving ability.

question: What is defensive driving?
options: a:Identifying dangerous situations and taking action to avoid accidents.,b:Getting ahead of poor drivers by driving aggressively.,c:Following the vehicle ahead at a close distance.
note: Defensive driving means recognizing hazards early and taking actions to prevent collisions.

question: What does a single broken white line down the center of a roadway indicate?
options: a:Lanes move in the same direction and drivers may change lanes or pass when safe.,b:Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is prohibited.,c:Lanes move in the same direction and passing is not permitted.
note: A dashed white line separates lanes moving in the same direction and may be crossed to change lanes when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following has priority over the others when directing traffic?
options: a:A steady red light,b:A stop sign,c:A police officer directing traffic.
note: Directions given by a traffic officer take precedence over signs, signals, and pavement markings.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless posted otherwise, what is the speed limit on narrow, winding mountain highways?
options: a:40 mph,b:20 mph,c:55 mph,d:70 mph
note: Colorado sets a lower default speed limit on narrow, winding mountain highways; unless posted otherwise the expected safe limit is 20 mph.

question: Which of the following about railroad crossings is true?
options: a:It is against the law to go around lowered gates at a crossing.,b:You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed to do so by a flagger or sign.,c:Not all railroad crossings have flashing lights and gates.,d:All of the above.
note: Obey all railroad crossing warnings: do not go around lowered gates, stop when directed, and be aware that not every crossing has lights or gates.

question: Driving while distracted by any activity typically:
options: a:Is never dangerous.,b:Causes drivers to react more slowly to hazards.,c:Causes drivers to drive faster.,d:Improves driver concentration.
note: Distracted driving reduces a driver's ability to notice and respond to hazards, increasing the likelihood of collisions.

question: If a driver accumulates the minimum of how many points in a 24-month period will their license be suspended?
options: a:12 points,b:18 points,c:20 points,d:24 points
note: In Colorado, accumulating 18 or more points within a 24-month period can result in suspension of your driver's license.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what is the correct response?
options: a:Overcorrect the steering.,b:Turn the steering wheel into the direction of the skid.,c:Turn your steering wheel into traffic.
note: If you start to skid, stay calm and steer in the direction of the skid to regain control.

question: If you are upset from an incident at work, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Turn the radio up loud to distract yourself.,b:Drive fast to release tension.,c:Take a few minutes to cool off before driving home.
note: If you are angry or upset, give yourself time to calm down before driving to avoid impaired judgment and aggressive behavior.

question: Before switching on the ignition, what safety step should you take?
options: a:Buckle your safety belt and make sure all passengers have buckled theirs.,b:Be sure only adult passengers have buckled their seat belts.,c:Be sure only child passengers have buckled their seat belts.,d:Only the driver needs to buckle a seat belt.
note: Develop a routine: before starting the engine, buckle your safety belt and ensure that all passengers are also properly restrained.

question: What do two solid yellow centerlines on the pavement mean?
options: a:Passing is allowed for drivers from both directions.,b:Passing is allowed at the top of a hill.,c:Passing is not allowed.
note: Two solid yellow lines separate opposing traffic and indicate passing is prohibited for drivers in either direction.

question: A steady yellow traffic signal indicates which light will appear next?
options: a:Flashing yellow,b:Steady green,c:Steady red,d:Flashing red
note: A steady yellow light warns that a steady red light is about to appear; prepare to stop if it is safe to do so.

question: Allow a larger space cushion than usual when stopped:
options: a:On an incline (uphill).,b:At an intersection.,c:At a stop sign.,d:When there is no traffic behind you.
note: When stopped on an uphill slope, leave more room ahead of you because the vehicle in front may roll backward when starting.

question: When a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light, who must yield?
options: a:Whoever started moving last.,b:The driver.,c:Whoever is slower at the moment.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians who are crossing the roadway, even if there is no traffic signal.

question: Which statement about winter driving is NOT true?
options: a:Checking antifreeze and windshield washer fluid is especially important during the winter.,b:Winter is the most difficult driving season.,c:Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.,d:Using snow tires can increase traction on slippery roads.
note: You should avoid using cruise control on snow, ice, rain, or fog. Winter requires extra caution, fluid checks, and consideration of snow tires.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you pull over and stop for an emergency vehicle with flashing lights?
options: a:Regardless of your direction.,b:Only if it is following you.,c:Only if it is approaching you from the opposite direction.
note: You must pull to the right edge of the road and stop for an emergency vehicle using lights and/or siren, regardless of whether it approaches from behind or ahead.

question: Guide signs (directional and mileage signs) are typically what color?
options: a:Green,b:Red,c:Yellow
note: Guide signs that provide route, directional, and mileage information are normally green with white lettering.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you signal before passing another vehicle?
options: a:After changing lanes.,b:Just before changing lanes.,c:At any time.
note: Signal early enough to let other drivers know your intentions before you start the passing maneuver.

question: If a pedestrian starts to cross in front of your vehicle, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrian.,b:Flash your lights to warn them.,c:Slow down and be prepared to stop.
note: Slow and be ready to stop any time pedestrians are on or near the roadway, especially where children may be present; always yield to them in crosswalks.

question: When preparing to change lanes, which of these is most important to check?
options: a:Signal your intentions ahead of the lane change.,b:Check your blind spot.,c:Make sure the lane is clear before entering.,d:Flash your headlights to warn others.
note: Always signal, check your mirrors, and quickly look over your shoulder to verify your blind spot is clear before changing lanes.

question: Which of the following is NOT an effect of drinking alcohol?
options: a:Your reflexes and reaction time speed up.,b:Your judgment of speed and distance is distorted.,c:You are less alert.
note: Alcohol impairs judgment, reaction time, perception of speed and distance, and alertness; it does not improve reflexes.

question: If your vehicle does not have ABS and you must stop quickly, what should you do?
options: a:Hold down the brake pedal.,b:Firmly pump your brakes.,c:Lightly tap the brakes.,d:Shift into neutral.
note: If your vehicle lacks ABS, pump the brakes firmly and repeatedly to slow quickly while maintaining steering control.

question: At night, which is the hardest to see?
options: a:Road signs.,b:Pedestrians.,c:Other motorists.,d:Lane markings.
note: Compared to signs and other roadside objects, pedestrians are generally the hardest to see at night.

question: A regulatory sign with a red circle and a slash through a symbol means:
options: a:That drivers should come to a complete stop.,b:The indicated action is forbidden.,c:That some drivers must yield to others.,d:That the lane is for high-occupancy vehicles only.
note: A red circle with a slash over a symbol indicates the action shown is prohibited (no turns, no U-turns, no parking, etc.).

question: If you discover a vehicle defect that could affect safe operation, you should:
options: a:Correct the defect as soon as possible.,b:Drive the vehicle at slower speeds until you can afford to fix it.,c:Ignore it until the next service appointment.
note: Any defect that could affect safe operation should be corrected as soon as possible before driving the vehicle.

question: If it starts to sleet or snow while you are driving, you should:
options: a:Keep your windshield and mirrors clear, increase your following distance, and approach other vehicles with caution.,b:Increase your speed to reach your destination sooner.,c:Follow closely to the vehicle ahead to use its traction.,d:Turn off your headlights to reduce glare.
note: In winter precipitation, keep windows and mirrors clear, slow down, and leave extra following distance since stopping distances increase.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a public road from a driveway or private road, you should:
options: a:Force your way into traffic.,b:Yield to drivers already on the public road.,c:Assume you have the right-of-way.
note: Yield to vehicles already on the public road and merge only when it is safe to do so.

question: How should you behave when approaching service or maintenance vehicles working on the roadway?
options: a:Treat them the same as any other vehicle.,b:Assume they will yield to you.,c:Yield and use extra caution around them.
note: Yield the right-of-way and use extra caution around maintenance and service vehicles; slow down and give them plenty of space.

question: If you borrow an unfamiliar vehicle, what should you do before driving it?
options: a:Assume it operates the same as your car.,b:Hide defects to avoid embarrassing the owner.,c:Familiarize yourself with the vehicle's controls and check for defects.
note: Before driving an unfamiliar vehicle, locate and test the lights, horn, wipers, gear selector, and brakes; fix any defects before driving.

question: Why is night driving typically more difficult than daytime driving?
options: a:It is more likely to be raining at night.,b:Visibility is reduced in the dark.,c:Cars overheat more quickly at night.
note: Night driving reduces your field of vision and increases the chance of glare from other vehicles; drive slower and use proper headlights.

question: If a transit bus is signaling to re-enter traffic after stopping, what must you do?
options: a:Honk to alert the bus driver.,b:Move to the left lane or slow to allow the bus to re-enter.,c:Expect the bus to yield to you.
note: Yield to transit vehicles re-entering traffic by changing lanes, slowing, or stopping to let them merge safely.

question: Pentagonal (five-sided) road signs indicate:
options: a:Speed limits.,b:School zones and school crossings.,c:No passing zones.,d:Railroad crossings.
note: Pentagonal signs identify school zones or school crossings; exercise extra caution for children and pedestrians in these areas.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane, two-way road you must:
options: a:Use the lane belonging to oncoming traffic to complete the pass when it is safe and legal to do so.,b:Stay entirely in your lane while overtaking.,c:Flash your headlights to demand the vehicle move over.,d:Use the shoulder to pass.
note: Passing on a two-lane, two-way road generally requires entering the oncoming lane; only pass when you have a clear view and it is legal and safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it illegal to drive slower than the posted speed limit?
options: a:When driving slowly disrupts the normal flow of traffic.,b:Only when driving in rural areas.,c:When in heavy traffic in a construction zone.
note: Driving so slowly that you impede the normal flow of traffic can be illegal and create safety hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct way to use a freeway exit ramp?
options: a:Slow down before entering the exit ramp.,b:Slow down once moving onto the exit ramp.,c:Keep your speed constant once in the exit ramp.
note: Do not decelerate on the mainline; instead, enter the exit ramp and then slow to the posted ramp speed once you are on the ramp.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is a good general rule to remember about passing other vehicles?
options: a:Pass on the right whenever possible.,b:Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only as needed.,c:Try to get to the front of any slow-moving traffic so you can see better.
note: Pass only when necessary and legal; driving with the flow of traffic reduces the number of lane changes and passing maneuvers, lowering collision risk.

question: How can a bicyclist who disobeys traffic laws be dealt with?
options: a:They have different rules and cannot be ticketed.,b:They can be ticketed.,c:They will always receive a warning instead of a ticket.
note: Bicyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as drivers and can be cited for violating traffic laws.

question: How should drivers treat a flashing red traffic light when approaching it?
options: a:Continue driving, as they have the right-of-way.,b:Stop if a police officer is nearby.,c:Treat it like a stop sign and stop.
note: Flashing red lights are used at dangerous intersections and must be treated like stop signs: come to a complete stop, then proceed when safe.

question: When making a turn, what should you do to your speed?
options: a:Increase your speed.,b:Maintain or reduce your speed as needed to maintain control.,c:Vary speed unpredictably.
note: Reduce your speed when turning so you can maintain control, stay in your lane, and react appropriately.

question: If an oncoming vehicle has its high beams on and is blinding you, what should you do?
options: a:Flash your lights to warn the other driver.,b:Look to the right side of the road until the vehicle passes.,c:Speed up to pass quickly.
note: When faced with blinding headlights, look down and to the right side of the road until the vehicle has passed to avoid temporary blindness.

question: What should you do if you become tired while driving?
options: a:Open the window to get some fresh air.,b:Stop driving and rest.,c:Drink coffee and keep driving.
note: Fatigue impairs driving similarly to alcohol. If you feel very tired, stop driving, rest, or find a safe place to sleep.

question: A leaking exhaust system can:
options: a:Cause excessive oil use.,b:Require your vehicle to have a tune-up sooner than usual.,c:Allow exhaust fumes into the passenger compartment and make you drowsy or cause death.,d:Increase brake wear.
note: A leaking exhaust can allow carbon monoxide and other toxic gases into the vehicle, which can make drivers drowsy or cause death; repair leaks promptly.
